scenario: ACH attempt times out (Unknown); provider query returns positive proof of non-receipt so the attempt moves to NotReceived
permitted_outcome: Grant returns to Funded and a new attempt with a new key may be created
prohibited_outcome: Grant left in PaymentInProgress with no live attempt; or a new attempt created while the grant still says payment in progress
governing_rules: GR diagram (PaymentInProgress->Funded only on Failed/Rejected); PA-1; PA-2
finding_description: Grant machine maps only attempt Failed/Rejected back to Funded. Attempt terminal states NotReceived, Recalled and Voided have no grant transition, so the grant is stranded in PaymentInProgress.

scenario: Donor asks to cancel while a wire is Accepted; GR-3 converts it to a recall; recall succeeds (attempt Recalled)
permitted_outcome: Grant leaves PaymentInProgress and the pending cancellation is decided (Canceled with reservation released or back to Funded)
prohibited_outcome: Grant stuck in PaymentInProgress; cancellation silently applied or silently forgotten
governing_rules: GR-3; GR-4; PA diagram RecallRequested->Recalled; CW-24
finding_description: No grant transition on attempt Recalled and no rule on whether the cancellation that triggered the recall is then applied automatically or needs a new sponsor decision.

scenario: Check issued (attempt Accepted per PA-4) is voided before presentment
permitted_outcome: Attempt Voided from Accepted; grant back to Funded or Canceled per policy
prohibited_outcome: Void impossible because the diagram only allows Settled->Voided; or check treated as Settled (cash out) before it cleared
finding_description: PA-4 says a check is Settled only when presented and cleared and Issued = Accepted, yet the diagram voids only from Settled 'before presentment'. The edge must be Accepted->Voided; as written a pre-presentment void is unreachable.

scenario: Attempt Unknown for 30 days; provider cannot give proof of absence; authorised human accepts duplicate-payment risk with a recovery plan (PA-2)
permitted_outcome: Unknown attempt moves to a terminal human-resolved state and a new attempt is permitted under recorded risk acceptance
prohibited_outcome: Human decision recorded but PA-1 still blocks any new attempt (Unknown is in the live set) so the grant can never be paid or canceled (GR-3)
finding_description: PA-2 allows a human decision to resolve Unknown but the attempt machine has no transition for it and PA-1 forbids a new attempt while any attempt is Unknown. GR-3 also forbids cancel. Result: permanent deadlock.

scenario: Payment provider ceases operations while one attempt is Unknown; no party can ever answer the query
permitted_outcome: Human resolution path (PA-2) with recovery claim against provider estate; grant re-payable via another provider
prohibited_outcome: Grant frozen forever in PaymentInProgress; or re-paid via second provider with no recorded decision
finding_description: Same deadlock as G-2 made permanent: provider-defined proof can never arrive, and FI-07 forbids releasing the reservation on Unknown, so the fund's capacity stays encumbered indefinitely.

scenario: Approved $3M grant exceeds the provider's per-transaction cap (attempt Prepared requires 'within caps')
permitted_outcome: Defined split-disbursement rule with sequential attempts summing exactly to the grant
prohibited_outcome: Grant unpayable; or caps bypassed
governing_rules: PA-1 (Settled-not-returned blocks next attempt); attempt Prepared precondition; RES PartiallyConsumed
finding_description: PA-1 counts Settled-not-returned as live, so a second attempt is never allowed after the first settles. Any grant above a rail cap is unpayable, and the reservation state PartiallyConsumed is unreachable.

scenario: Sponsor policy allows split disbursement; multi-source grant pays line A now while gated line B waits (FI-13)
permitted_outcome: First tranche paid; second tranche paid later; reservation PartiallyConsumed then Consumed
prohibited_outcome: Second tranche blocked forever by PA-1; or PA-1 suspended ad hoc
finding_description: FI-13 and the reservation model contemplate split disbursement but PA-1 makes it impossible. PA-1 needs to be per tranche (cumulative settled <= grant amount) rather than one attempt per grant.

scenario: Attempt is Authorized (released) but not yet Submitted when the sponsor cancels the grant
permitted_outcome: Cancel voids the Authorized attempt atomically; submission later re-checks grant state and refuses
prohibited_outcome: Grant Canceled and reservation released while the Authorized attempt remains and is later submitted, paying a canceled grant
governing_rules: GR-3 (blocks cancel only for Submitted/Unknown/Accepted); PA-1; SM-6
finding_description: The attempt machine has no exit from Prepared or Authorized (no Abandoned/Superseded), GR-3 permits cancellation while an Authorized attempt exists, and SM-6's re-check list (authority, eligibility, holds, freshness) does not include grant state or reservation existence.

scenario: Recipient's verified bank profile changes while an attempt is Authorized against the old profile; SM-6 freshness check fails at submission
permitted_outcome: Attempt abandoned with reason; new attempt against new profile
prohibited_outcome: Attempt submitted to stale account; or attempt stuck in Authorized and PA-1 blocks a new one
finding_description: Failing an SM-6 re-check has nowhere to go: Authorized has no terminal exit, and PA-1 counts Authorized as live, so the grant cannot get a new attempt.

scenario: Provider reports Failed before settlement; grant returns to Funded and a second attempt is created; three days later the bank statement shows the first payment settled
permitted_outcome: Contradicting evidence opens a double-payment case and blocks further attempts; recovery from recipient
prohibited_outcome: Two payments with no detection; or the ledger edits the terminal Failed attempt
governing_rules: PA-1; PA diagram (Failed terminal); FI-29; SM-0
finding_description: PA-1 treats provider-reported Failed (and Recalled, NotReceived, Returned) as safe-to-retry terminal states. Unlike PA-2 it requires no proof of non-processing, and no rule handles later evidence contradicting a terminal attempt state.

scenario: ACH return processed (attempt Returned, fund re-credited, re-pay attempt submitted); originating bank's return is dishonored as untimely and the funds go back to the charity
permitted_outcome: Linked correction re-establishes the first payment as Settled; re-pay recalled or recovery case
prohibited_outcome: Charity receives the grant twice; fund double-debited with no case
finding_description: Returned is terminal in the attempt machine; dishonored or contested returns reverse it. With PA-1 unlocked by Returned, the re-pay creates a double payment that no rule detects.

scenario: Return notification arrives before the settlement notification (out-of-order provider events)
permitted_outcome: Return accepted as implying settlement; both facts recorded with effective times; reservation handled once
prohibited_outcome: Return rejected because Accepted->Returned is not a legal transition; or settlement processed after return re-consumes the reservation
finding_description: The attempt machine assumes observations arrive in causal order. No rule says whether an observation implies its predecessors or how a late predecessor is reconciled after a successor has been applied.

scenario: Provider API proves NotReceived; a new attempt is created; next day the bank statement shows a debit for the first attempt
permitted_outcome: Break (FI-29); new attempt blocked pending resolution; recall of one payment
prohibited_outcome: Both payments proceed because PA-1 was already satisfied
finding_description: FI-29 opens a break but nothing makes a break on an attempt block the other attempts on the same grant; PA-1 has already been satisfied by the contradicted terminal state.

scenario: Attempt Unknown; after 48 hours the query finds nothing; the same attempt is retried with the same key but the provider's idempotency window is 24 hours
permitted_outcome: Retry allowed only within the provider's dedup window; beyond it, treat as PA-2 decision
prohibited_outcome: Provider treats the retry as a new payment; double payment while PA-3 is satisfied
finding_description: PA-3 assumes the provider honours the key forever. Real provider dedup windows are finite and versioned. The retry rule must be bounded by the provider's contractual key-retention window [C GAP-002].

scenario: ACH file of 400 entries times out at transmission; provider later acknowledges the file but rejects 3 entries
permitted_outcome: File-level Unknown fans out to 400 attempt-level Unknowns; file acknowledgement resolves 397; 3 Rejected
prohibited_outcome: 397 treated as failed and re-sent; or 3 rejects missed because the file was 'accepted'
finding_description: The attempt model is per payment, but rails submit files/batches. No rule links batch state to attempt state, defines a batch idempotency key, or handles partial batch acceptance.

scenario: Operator manually re-transmits the same ACH file after a timeout without querying
permitted_outcome: Re-transmission blocked while any attempt in the file is Unknown
prohibited_outcome: Every entry paid twice; PA-3 keys never seen because file-level dedup is by file name/ID
finding_description: PA-3's per-attempt key does not protect a file-level resend through a channel that dedups on file identity. Batch transmission needs its own idempotency and query-before-resend rule.

scenario: Provider debits the sponsor's account at acceptance (pre-funding), then fails before settlement (insolvency); attempt Failed
permitted_outcome: Grant held; provider receivable recorded; cash not treated as back in the fund
prohibited_outcome: Grant returns to Funded with reservation intact and is paid again from cash that already left
governing_rules: GR diagram PaymentInProgress->Funded; FI-17; fact 9 'Provider acceptance moves money'
finding_description: The facts table says acceptance moves money, but reservation consumption and cash reduction occur only at settlement (FI-17, GR-4). Funds held by a provider or intermediary between acceptance and settlement are not modelled; Failed is assumed to mean cash never left.

scenario: Grant paid through a disbursement intermediary that pools and pays charities monthly; intermediary receives funds then delays or fails
permitted_outcome: Settled-to-intermediary distinguished from received-by-recipient; status does not say 'Paid to recipient'
prohibited_outcome: Donor sees 'Paid to [Recipient] on D' while the charity has nothing; loss bearer undefined
governing_rules: FI fact 10 (funds at recipient's bank); status vocabulary Disbursed label
finding_description: Settlement is defined as funds at the recipient's bank, but intermediated rails settle to a third party first. No state or rule covers the intermediary leg or its failure.

scenario: Grant Funded at custodian; the sweep wire from custodian to the disbursement bank fails; payment is submitted from the bank account
permitted_outcome: Payment submission checks cash at the paying account (constrained ancestor) and waits
prohibited_outcome: Overdraft at disbursement bank; or provider reject misread as grant failure
finding_description: Funded means cash settled at the custodian, but payments leave from a different bank account. The custodian-to-bank cash movement is not a lifecycle step, and FI-05 checks ancestors at reservation, not at submission.

scenario: Wire settles with a $25 intermediary bank fee deducted; provider reports settled amount of grant minus 25
permitted_outcome: Defined fee bearer; reservation consumed in full or remainder released by explicit rule; recipient shortfall handled
prohibited_outcome: Reservation remainder left Active forever (Stranded) because GR-4/FI-07 allow release only on cancel/decline/consumption
finding_description: FI-17 consumes the reservation by the settled amount X and assumes X equals the grant. No rule covers settled amount different from the reservation (fees, FX buffer remainder, over-debit), so a remainder is stranded by construction.

scenario: Returned wire comes back net of return fees ($9,950 of $10,000)
permitted_outcome: Re-pay at full fixed amount with the $50 drawn by explicit policy; or sponsor absorbs
prohibited_outcome: Re-reservation of $9,950 and re-pay of $9,950 under a grant fixed at $10,000
finding_description: FI-19 re-establishes the reservation 'from that cash' and GR-1 fixes the amount; the two diverge when the returned amount is less than the grant. Who bears the difference is undefined.

scenario: Check uncashed past state dormancy; Escheated is required but not drawn
permitted_outcome: Escheat state with defined reservation consumption, liability transfer and donor label
prohibited_outcome: Reservation Active for years (consumption only at Disbursed); FUND-1 blocks fund closure; donor sees 'Payment in progress' indefinitely
governing_rules: PA-4; FI-21; GR-4; FUND-1; status vocabulary
finding_description: Check lifecycle is not closed: Escheated has no attempt or grant edges, reservation treatment is undefined, and no label exists for aged, voided-for-escheat or escheated checks. Void-and-recredit before dormancy may itself conflict with unclaimed-property law [C].

scenario: Outstanding issued check: FI-21 removes the amount from fund cash (liability) while the reservation stays Active until clearing
permitted_outcome: Amount counted once against capacity
prohibited_outcome: Capacity C reduced twice (V lowered by the liability and R still includes the reservation)
finding_description: FI-21 and GR-4 together double-count an issued check against capacity. Conservative (understates C), but it misstates available-to-recommend (FI-06) for every outstanding check.

scenario: Donor withdraws the recommendation while the grant is AwaitingHumanDecision with a specialist
permitted_outcome: Grant record closes (Withdrawn/Abandoned) atomically with the recommendation; specialist cannot approve
prohibited_outcome: Grant stays in review; specialist approves; a grant nobody recommends is reserved and paid
governing_rules: REC-2; Grant diagram (no UnderReview/AwaitingHumanDecision exit except Approved/Declined); CW-24
finding_description: The Grant object exists from UnderReview while the Recommendation is still Submitted, but the grant machine has no transition for withdrawal. Withdrawal leaves an orphan that can still be approved.

scenario: Donor edits a Submitted recommendation (Superseded) after the grant entered UnderReview
permitted_outcome: Old grant closes as superseded; only the new recommendation proceeds
prohibited_outcome: Two grants in review for one intent; both approved and paid
governing_rules: REC transitions Submitted->Superseded; Grant diagram; REC-4
finding_description: Supersession on the request side has no counterpart on the grant side. REC-4 duplicate detection is a flag only and does not cover the requester's own superseded version.

scenario: Donor removes an advisor's capability after the sponsor approved that advisor's grant and before payment
permitted_outcome: Defined rule: SM-6 re-checks sponsor release authority only; requester authority governed by GR-8/sponsor policy
prohibited_outcome: Grant silently blocked at submission by a requester-authority check; or paid with no review where policy requires one
finding_description: SM-6 says 're-check authority' at payment submission without saying whose. If it is the requester's, it contradicts GR-8 (approved grants are not auto-canceled when the donor's authority ends); if it is the releaser's only, the catalog's Auth row ('requester capability ... re-check at payment submission') is wrong.

scenario: The staff member who approved under DoA leaves the sponsor (authority revoked) before release
permitted_outcome: Approval stands (sponsor act at decision time) unless policy requires re-approval; release authority checked at submission
prohibited_outcome: Approved grants of departed staff all blocked; or nothing re-checked
finding_description: Same SM-6 ambiguity from the sponsor side: whether an approver's later loss of authority invalidates approvals already given is not decided.

scenario: Fund Suspended (sponsor policy hold) while a grant is in Returned awaiting re-pay
permitted_outcome: Re-pay held, because the grant is about to move money again
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay proceeds because GR-7 holds only grants 'not yet PaymentInProgress'
finding_description: GR-7 scopes the fund-level hold by lifecycle position ('not yet PaymentInProgress'). A Returned grant has passed that point but is about to pay again, so literally it escapes the hold.

scenario: Fund Frozen under a sanctions order while a grant is Returned awaiting re-pay
permitted_outcome: No re-pay; returned cash stays blocked
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay from a frozen fund
governing_rules: Fund Frozen definition (§6: nothing moves); FUND-2; SM-6 hold re-check

scenario: Return arrives while the fund is over-committed (R > V - H)
permitted_outcome: Explicit rule: a return re-establishes its own reservation from its own cash, exempt from FI-12 refusal
prohibited_outcome: Return cannot be re-reserved (FI-12 refuses new reservations) so returned cash becomes free capacity for others
finding_description: FI-19 re-establishes a reservation on return; FI-12 refuses all new reservations while over-committed. Both cannot hold; the exemption must be explicit.

scenario: Grant return arrives after the fund is Closed (ClosedWithResidualRecovery)
permitted_outcome: Defined destination per policy; grant decision (re-pay to charity vs trailing receipt) made explicitly
prohibited_outcome: Fund re-opened Active (FI-35) to re-credit and re-pay; or the charity silently loses the grant
finding_description: FI-19 sends returned cash to the fund and re-pays the grant; FI-35 sends late returns to a trailing-receipt destination and forbids re-opening. Whether the sponsor still owes the charity the grant is undecided.

scenario: Forward NAV falls between order and strike; FI-14 draws the shortfall from the fund but the fund has no remaining capacity
permitted_outcome: One rule decides: exact amount (FI-14) or sponsor decision case with partial (FI-12)
prohibited_outcome: Recipient paid less without a rule; or fund silently negative
finding_description: FI-14 guarantees the grant receives exactly its fixed amount; FI-12 lists 'partial' as a sponsor option; FI-13 forbids partial payment unless split disbursement is allowed. The three disagree on whether the fixed amount can be reduced.

scenario: Sponsor chooses 'partial' under FI-12 for an approved unfunded grant
permitted_outcome: Defined amendment (reduce fixed amount, new version, donor notice) or cancel-and-regrant
prohibited_outcome: Fixed amount edited in place, contradicting GR-1 and SM-0
finding_description: The grant machine has no amount-amendment transition, so the FI-12 'partial' option cannot be executed without an edit that GR-1/SM-0 prohibit.

scenario: Approval not atomic with reservation (OD-06); reservation fails capacity; grant Approved and held 'insufficient capacity'; two weeks later capacity returns and a newer grant reserves first
permitted_outcome: Defined queue: held approvals reserve before new ones, or expire with notice
prohibited_outcome: Older approved grant starved indefinitely; donor sees 'On hold - sponsor review'
governing_rules: FI-05; FI-08; FI-12; status vocabulary hold reason classes
finding_description: There is no queue, priority or expiry for approved-but-unreserved grants, and the hold reason classes have no 'awaiting available funds'. FI-12 funds in approval order only when over-committed, not in this case.

scenario: January recurring instance held for capacity; February instance due; capacity restored enough for one
permitted_outcome: Defined order (oldest first, or policy)
prohibited_outcome: Newest instance reserves and the older one remains held without rule
finding_description: CW-03 says a held instance does not stop the series but gives no ordering between held and new instances.

scenario: Back-office approval command carries an effective_at earlier than a competing reservation's recorded time
permitted_outcome: Priority determined by recorded serialization time; effective_at cannot reorder priority
prohibited_outcome: Backdated effective time used for 'approval order' (FI-12) to jump the queue
governing_rules: FI-08; FI-12; SM-1; core command envelope effective_at
finding_description: FI-08 orders by reservation serialization, FI-12 by 'approval order', CW-03 by reservation time; the command envelope lets the client supply effective_at. Which clock defines priority is not stated.

scenario: Scheduler outage of 3 days; on recovery a catch-up job creates instances while the original stalled run also completes
permitted_outcome: One instance per template-period (natural idempotency key)
prohibited_outcome: Two instances for the same period with different keys; both approved and paid
finding_description: No rule makes (template, period) the idempotency key of a recurring instance. REC-4 only flags duplicates, and two system-generated instances would both pass every check.

scenario: Scheduler down across a month boundary so January's instance never fired
permitted_outcome: Policy: catch up or skip, with donor notice
prohibited_outcome: Implementation choice; silent skip or silent double in February
finding_description: Missed-run semantics (catch-up vs skip) for recurring instances are undecided.

scenario: Monthly recurring grant due on the 31st; February; due date on a weekend; donor in Pacific time, sponsor in Eastern; DST change at the scheduled hour
permitted_outcome: Defined roll convention, business-day calendar and time zone for due dates
prohibited_outcome: Instance fires twice on DST fall-back or not at all in February
governing_rules: FI-09 ('at the instance's due date'); CW-03
finding_description: FI-09 reserves at 'the due date' without defining the calendar, roll convention or time zone of a due date.

scenario: Settlement observed 3 days late; the Final window is computed from the effective settlement date in business days
permitted_outcome: Final computed from effective settlement date on the rail's banking-day calendar; recorded time kept separately
prohibited_outcome: Final computed from recorded time (window wrongly extended) or from calendar days (wrongly shortened)
finding_description: GR-5 says Final is rail-specific and time-based but not which clock (effective vs recorded) or calendar (banking days, which holidays).

scenario: Attempt goes Unknown Friday after cutoff before a three-day holiday; Unknown-unresolved SLA is in wall-clock hours and escalates while the provider query desk is closed
permitted_outcome: SLA measured in provider business hours; escalation does not push toward a PA-2 duplicate-risk decision
prohibited_outcome: Pressure to make a PA-2 human decision before the provider can answer
governing_rules: PA-2; CW-01 Failure row (Unknown unresolved > SLA)
finding_description: The Unknown SLA clock basis is undefined; a wall-clock SLA biases toward premature PA-2 risk acceptance.

scenario: Payment settles Dec 31 (effective) but the observation is recorded Jan 3 after the December period closed
permitted_outcome: Posting in January with effective date Dec 31 and a defined rule for which year's grants-paid report includes it
prohibited_outcome: Posting into the closed period (FI-01); or the grant omitted from both years' reports
finding_description: Assignment of late-observed settlements to accounting periods and to annual grant reporting (990 / Schedule D) is undefined. FI-27 covers fee restatement only.

scenario: An attempt is Unknown at fiscal year-end
permitted_outcome: Defined financial-statement treatment (cash with contingent liability or disbursed with receivable) [C]
prohibited_outcome: Ad hoc treatment at close
finding_description: The model keeps the reservation and cash on Unknown (correct operationally) but gives no reporting treatment for an Unknown at period end.

scenario: Grant approved at 23:30 Pacific on Dec 31 (07:30 UTC Jan 1); donor statement lists 'grants approved in 2026'
permitted_outcome: One reporting time zone per sponsor, stated on statements
prohibited_outcome: Donor statement and sponsor ledger disagree on the year
finding_description: Dates shown to donors and used in reports ('Paid ... on D', approval date) have no defined time zone.

scenario: Donor amends a recurring template's amount while the current instance is Reserved
permitted_outcome: Amendment applies to future instances only; the reserved instance keeps its fixed amount
prohibited_outcome: Reserved instance edited in place
finding_description: The recurring template has no lifecycle (amend, pause, resume). How amendments affect instances in flight is not stated, though GR-1 implies the answer.

scenario: Recipient revoked so the series is suspended; IRS later reinstates the charity retroactively
permitted_outcome: Resume requires requester confirmation; missed periods not caught up silently
prohibited_outcome: Series auto-resumes and catches up all missed instances
finding_description: No resume rule after series suspension.

scenario: Template created by the donor's agent under a confirm-required rule; each instance is system-generated
permitted_outcome: Defined: instance inherits the confirmed template, or each instance needs confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Instances bypass AwaitingRequesterConfirmation because no explicit submit exists
finding_description: Recurring instances do not fit the recommendation machine (no explicit submit or preview hash). Who the requester is and whether confirmation rules re-apply per instance are undecided.

scenario: Donor requests cancellation during Accepted; recall fails (RecallRequested->Settled)
permitted_outcome: Cancellation request closes with outcome 'could not be stopped - paid on D'
prohibited_outcome: Donor sees 'cancellation requested - payment may already be on its way' indefinitely
finding_description: GrantCancellationRequested has no lifecycle (pending, granted, refused, overtaken by settlement) and no dimension in the status vocabulary.

scenario: Donor requests cancellation of a Funded grant; sponsor refuses (its discretion)
permitted_outcome: Donor told the request was not granted and why (class)
prohibited_outcome: No representation; grant shows 'Approved' and donor assumes cancel succeeded
finding_description: Refusal of a cancellation request is not representable.

scenario: Donor asks to cancel while the grant is in Funding (liquidation ordered)
permitted_outcome: Defined: wait for Funded or FundingShortfall then cancel; or cancel with liquidation proceeds returned to fund
prohibited_outcome: Request accepted by CW-24 ('Approved..Funded sponsor decides') but the machine has no Funding->Canceled edge
finding_description: CW-24 says the sponsor may cancel anywhere from Approved to Funded; the state machine omits Funding->Canceled.

scenario: Multi-source grant: line A liquidated and settled, line B gated; FundingShortfall; sponsor cancels
permitted_outcome: Line A cash returned to fund and reinvested per policy; realised gain/loss recorded
prohibited_outcome: Cash from line A left idle or attributed to no one
finding_description: Partly-funded state is not modelled, and the destination/reinvestment of proceeds already liquidated for a canceled grant is unspecified (FI-19 covers returns only).

scenario: Funded grant held 6 months for eligibility review; its cash sits uninvested
permitted_outcome: Policy decides whether to reinvest or keep cash and discloses to donor
prohibited_outcome: Unbounded idle cash with no rule
finding_description: No rule for cash allocated to a grant that is held for a long time.

scenario: ACH settles day 1; return window open until day 60
permitted_outcome: Label qualified, e.g. 'Paid on D - final after return window' or as GR-5 requires
prohibited_outcome: Unqualified 'Paid to [Recipient] on D' before Final
governing_rules: GR-5; status vocabulary §1 Payment row and §2 item 4; CW-01 User-visible
finding_description: GR-5 forbids saying 'paid' before Final without a qualifier; the status vocabulary shows 'Paid to [Recipient] on D' at Disbursed and hides Final ('Paid remains'); CW-01 only forbids 'paid' before Disbursed. The three documents disagree.

scenario: Grant Returned, sponsor then cancels it (funds back to fund)
permitted_outcome: Headline 'Canceled' with note that the payment was returned
prohibited_outcome: Headline 'Returned - updating payment details' forever and charity asked to re-enroll
governing_rules: Status vocabulary §2 (Returned priority 3 above Canceled priority 8)
finding_description: Headline derivation ranks payment dimensions above terminal decision dimensions, so a canceled grant keeps an action-implying headline.

scenario: Sanctions-screening hold added to a grant whose attempt is Accepted (money committed)
permitted_outcome: Headline shows both: payment in progress and review
prohibited_outcome: 'On hold' headline implies the money was stopped when it was not
finding_description: Hold has top priority even when the hold cannot affect an in-flight payment, which misleads donors.

scenario: Sponsor notifies the charity of the award at approval; charity commits spending; sponsor later cancels (over-commitment or new policy)
permitted_outcome: Policy defines when recipient is notified and whether the grant is conditional until payment [C ASC 958]
prohibited_outcome: Unconditional promise communicated then canceled with no accounting/legal treatment
governing_rules: FI fact 2; GR diagram Approved->Canceled; CW-01 Outputs (recipient notices)
finding_description: The model treats approval as revocable until payment. If recipients are notified at approval, the sponsor may have recorded an unconditional promise to give; cancellation then has accounting and possibly legal consequences that are not modelled.

scenario: Verified-channel bank change was itself compromised; payment Settled to attacker; legitimate charity unpaid
permitted_outcome: Recovery case; replacement grant funded per a predefined loss-bearing policy
prohibited_outcome: Donor fund silently charged twice; or no replacement because PA-1 blocks re-pay
governing_rules: PA-1; §10 Compensation row ('new grant if needed'); GR-6
finding_description: The compensation rule creates a new grant but not who funds it (donor fund vs sponsor operating funds/insurance) or whether it needs a fresh recommendation and capacity.

scenario: Check stolen and cashed with a forged endorsement; attempt Settled
permitted_outcome: Bank claim; replacement funded per loss policy
prohibited_outcome: Charity never paid; donor sees 'Paid'
finding_description: Same gap as G-27 for checks.

scenario: Benefit-risk model flag places a hold; the same model re-runs on new data and the flag goes Superseded (§8), releasing the hold
permitted_outcome: Hold release requires a deterministic rule or authorised human
prohibited_outcome: Model effectively releases a hold
finding_description: §8 lets a flag be Superseded when 'a rule re-ran ... and no longer fires'. If the raising 'rule' is a model run, this is a model-driven release, which SM-5 forbids.

scenario: 10% grant fixed at approval using a struck NAV that is later restated beyond materiality (FI-28)
permitted_outcome: Defined: fixed amount stands (GR-1) and the error is a fund-level NAV-error effect, or amount corrected by cancel-and-regrant
prohibited_outcome: Grant amount silently re-computed under restatement re-processing; or donor never told the fixing basis was wrong
finding_description: FI-28 restatement 're-processes unit transactions'; GR-1 says the amount never moves. Whether a fixing is a unit transaction subject to restatement is not decided.

scenario: Three-way match completes at T+2; Final occurs at T+60
permitted_outcome: Reconciliation recorded as an orthogonal fact
prohibited_outcome: Reconciliation cannot be recorded until Final because the machine sequences Final->Reconciled
governing_rules: Grant diagram; status vocabulary (Finality/reconciliation as a separate dimension); fact 12
finding_description: The grant machine linearises finality and reconciliation; the status vocabulary and fact 12 treat them as independent.

scenario: Same late return: grant A was Final (not yet reconciled) and goes to Returned with re-pay; grant B was Reconciled and gets only a child ReturnCase
permitted_outcome: Same business outcome regardless of back-office reconciliation timing
prohibited_outcome: Grant B's charity cannot be re-paid without a new grant
governing_rules: Grant diagram (Final->Returned); SM-0; CW-06 Failure row; TVS-017
finding_description: Re-pay availability depends on whether reconciliation happened to run first. TVS-017 covers recording; this is the re-pay path difference.

scenario: Residual sweep (100% grant): fees accrue through closure date; closure date is after the sweep settles
permitted_outcome: Fee cut-off date fixed before residual fixing; trailing fee goes to FI-35 destination
prohibited_outcome: Sweep amount wrong because fees keep accruing after fixing; or fund closure blocked by fee balance
finding_description: FI-15 fixes the sweep after all fees through closing; FUND-1 requires fees through the closure date, which follows the sweep. Circular unless a fee cut-off is defined.

scenario: Sponsor declines a grant that is Reserved
permitted_outcome: Not reachable: Declined only precedes Approved
prohibited_outcome: n/a
governing_rules: GR-4 ('Declined (if reserved)'); FI-05 (reservation at or after approval)
finding_description: GR-4 refers to a reserved Declined grant, which the machine cannot produce. Spec hygiene only.

scenario: Sponsor cancel command and settlement observation race on a grant in PaymentInProgress
permitted_outcome: Settlement wins by revision; cancel rejected as stale; donor told payment completed
prohibited_outcome: Both Canceled and Disbursed

scenario: While the attempt is Unknown the charity emails 'we received it'
permitted_outcome: Stays Unknown; email attached as evidence; provider query continues
prohibited_outcome: Attempt moved to Settled on recipient's say-so

scenario: Donor died (effective) before a one-off grant was approved; death reported after approval
permitted_outcome: Grant flagged for review; completion per sponsor policy
prohibited_outcome: Automatic reversal; or ignored

scenario: Percentage recommendation spends 3 weeks in AwaitingHumanDecision while NAV rises 15%
permitted_outcome: Fixed at approval on latest struck NAV; donor shown estimate vs fixed
prohibited_outcome: Amount fixed at submission or drifting after approval

scenario: 10% of fund value V where V includes a provisional contribution that later reverses
permitted_outcome: Fixed amount stands; reservation already limited to C which excluded provisional value; reversal handled by FI-23
prohibited_outcome: Grant amount re-computed after fixing

scenario: Pool-level aggregated liquidation order fails at the custodian for all grants in Funding
permitted_outcome: Each grant enters FundingShortfall; re-plan or hold
prohibited_outcome: Grants marked Funded on order rather than settlement

scenario: Custodian busts a liquidation trade after the grant was paid
permitted_outcome: Fund absorbs via FI-28 correction; over-commitment case if needed; recipient unaffected
prohibited_outcome: Recovery sought from the charity

scenario: Charity tells the sponsor before payment that it will not accept the grant
permitted_outcome: Sponsor cancels; reservation released
prohibited_outcome: Payment sent anyway

scenario: R03 return; charity re-enrols a new account through the verified channel; cooling-off applies
permitted_outcome: Re-pay waits for cooling-off; H after N days
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay to unverified or cooling-off profile
governing_rules: Attempt Prepared precondition; CW-06 Decisions; GR Returned->Funded

scenario: Charity revoked while grant is Returned awaiting re-pay
permitted_outcome: Re-pay blocked at submission by eligibility re-check
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay to revoked charity

scenario: Charity refunds a paid grant by mistake and asks for it to be re-sent
permitted_outcome: New grant (PA-1 blocks a new attempt on the settled one); refund handled as receipt
prohibited_outcome: New attempt on the original grant

scenario: Wire recall requested after settlement because of a fraud indicator
permitted_outcome: Recovery case with human authority, not an attempt transition
prohibited_outcome: Attempt edited back to RecallRequested

scenario: Model-placed hold on a Reserved grant stays unreviewed for weeks, encumbering capacity
permitted_outcome: Flag escalates past SLA; sponsor can cancel; reservation not released by time
prohibited_outcome: Reservation released on timeout

scenario: Specialist approves while evidence-triggered rule re-run moves the grant back to UnderReview
permitted_outcome: One command wins by revision; the other is rejected as stale
prohibited_outcome: Approval applied to a superseded revision

scenario: Co-advisor removes the advisor who authored a recurring template
permitted_outcome: Series suspended at next instance
prohibited_outcome: Instances continue under the removed advisor's authority

scenario: Return arrives after the grant was Reconciled at month-end
permitted_outcome: Child ReturnCase; reconciliation break
prohibited_outcome: Edit reconciled grant

scenario: Check presented after it was voided
permitted_outcome: Bank stop; recovery case
prohibited_outcome: Double payment

scenario: Unknown payment shown as failed; donor re-recommends
permitted_outcome: 'Confirming payment status' copy; duplicate flag
prohibited_outcome: Two payments

scenario: Recurring instance and an extraordinary grant compete for the same capacity on one day
permitted_outcome: Reservation order; loser held
prohibited_outcome: Both paid

scenario: Fund migrated from incumbent with its field-of-interest restriction held only as free text in a PDF; advisor recommends a grant the day after cutover outside that field
permitted_outcome: Fund enters a defined post-migration state with grants held until MIG-04 validation and AG-03 structured restriction approval are complete
prohibited_outcome: Grant approved because the migrated fund arrived as Active and FI-32 had no structured restriction to test
finding_description: Migrated funds have no defined entry state. They bypass CW-09/EST-11 activation gates, and nothing says which capabilities stay held until MIG-04 validation of agreements, restrictions and authority is complete.

scenario: Incumbent export lists a service contact (CPA) with role 'advisor'; signed agreement names only the donor
permitted_outcome: Authority derived from validated signed agreement (MIG-04); CPA gets no recommend capability; discrepancy case
prohibited_outcome: Imported contact role becomes an advisory privilege

scenario: Incumbent administrator becomes insolvent mid-migration; export is incomplete and opening balances cannot be reconciled to statements before year-end grant season
permitted_outcome: A defined degraded mode: provisional opening balances with haircut and capacity limits and an explicit owner decision
prohibited_outcome: Live money movement on unreconciled balances; or an indefinite freeze with no rule while donors' grants stall
finding_description: Migration gating (MIG-06 dual run; MIG-09) assumes a cooperative incumbent. There are no rules for a failed or uncooperative incumbent: provisional opening balances, capacity limits, and who may approve operating before reconciliation.

scenario: Incumbent issued a check pre-cutover that is still uncashed; post-cutover the donor sees no payment in the new portal and re-recommends the same grant
permitted_outcome: Incumbent attempts imported as payment-attempt records with provider/bank references so PA-1 blocks a second attempt; duplicate flag (REC-4)
prohibited_outcome: Second payment while the incumbent check is still live
finding_description: Incumbent in-flight items (open payment attempts and uncashed checks, provisional contributions, issued acknowledgments, open flags and cases, events still arriving at the incumbent's bank) are not mapped into the refined state machines. PA-1, CON-2, FLAG-1 and FUND-1 cannot be enforced across the cutover boundary.

scenario: ACH contribution pulled by incumbent 10 days before cutover returns R10 to the incumbent's bank account after cutover; incumbent already issued the acknowledgment and the units were migrated
permitted_outcome: Return routed to the new administrator; units cancelled per FI-23; acknowledgment corrected by the sponsor (CW-28); receivable if spent (CON-3)
prohibited_outcome: Incumbent absorbs or ignores the return; migrated units remain; acknowledgment stands
finding_description: Same gap as X-2: returns and other events still arriving on the incumbent's rails after cutover have no routing rule, and migrated contributions carry no Provisional or Final state.

scenario: Recurring grant templates migrated; one template's author lost advisory privilege at the incumbent last year (not reflected in export)
permitted_outcome: Per-instance authority re-check (CW-03 precondition) after MIG-04 validation; instance held
prohibited_outcome: First instance fires on imported template

scenario: Cutover on July 1; Form 990 Schedule D for the year needs incumbent Jan-Jun and new Jul-Dec contribution and grant aggregates
permitted_outcome: Historical import with lineage and continuous historical query (MIG-05; MIG-08); one sponsor-level aggregate
prohibited_outcome: Double counting or omission of the incumbent half-year

scenario: Incumbent bills fees quarterly in arrears; cutover mid-quarter; incumbent debits a full quarter fee after the new system started accruing
permitted_outcome: Accrued unpaid fee liability reconciled in opening balance; proration; dispute case; adjustment entry
prohibited_outcome: Fund charged twice for the same days

scenario: Open potential sanctions match on a donor at the incumbent is not in the export (incumbent closed queue at contract end)
permitted_outcome: Open flags imported as Raised or donor re-screened at cutover with case carried forward
prohibited_outcome: Flag silently lost; grants proceed
finding_description: Open flags and cases are among the in-flight items X-2 leaves unmapped. FLAG-1 (flags never expire) has no import rule.

scenario: Cutover rolled back after 3 days during which the new system accepted contributions and paid grants
permitted_outcome: Forward recovery only for executed money movements; rollback limited to non-financial state
prohibited_outcome: Rollback that erases executed payments or issued acknowledgments

scenario: Donor wires $250k to the sponsor while the fund application is UnderReview; screening later causes the application to be rejected
permitted_outcome: Receipt held in owned suspense; units not issued; acknowledgment and disposition (refund vs other) decided under a stated rule [C]
prohibited_outcome: Units issued to a non-active fund; money returned without legal review of a completed gift; receipt left without an acknowledgment decision
finding_description: Contributions received before activation, or for an application later rejected, have no defined lifecycle. FI-04 suspense only gives the cash an owner. Gift date, acknowledgment, unit issuance at activation and disposition after rejection are undefined, and a completed gift may not be refundable [C].

scenario: Stock delivered by DTC with a valid intent reference to a fund in Approved (not Active); fund activates 3 weeks later after a 10% market drop
permitted_outcome: Defined rule for holding or liquidating the pre-activation asset and for the NAV at which units issue; acknowledgment gift date = receipt (WF-02)
prohibited_outcome: Units issued at the receipt-date NAV by ad hoc choice; or the loss is assigned arbitrarily
finding_description: X-3 for in-kind gifts: investment exposure between receipt and activation has no owner.

scenario: Eight months after activation, one co-donor's e-signature on the fund agreement is found to have been applied by the spouse; grants already paid
permitted_outcome: Case; fund Suspended pending re-execution; past grants reviewed as sponsor acts; legal review [C]
prohibited_outcome: Fund treated as validly established with no review; or paid grants automatically unwound
finding_description: Retroactive invalidation of an acceptance or activation prerequisite (agreement execution evidence, KYC, source of funds, contribution taint) has no lifecycle. SM-0 child records exist for grants. Fund and Contribution have no equivalent, and acknowledgment status is undefined.

scenario: Donor identity found to be synthetic after $500k contributed and $300k granted
permitted_outcome: Fund Frozen or Suspended (H); reporting obligations [C]; contributions reviewed for legal void; grants via post-payment review
prohibited_outcome: Automatic reversal of grants; or unit cancellation without a decision
finding_description: X-4: no transition models revoking a fund's establishment after money moved.

scenario: Applicant dies after signing the agreement but before sponsor acceptance; application names a successor
permitted_outcome: Activation gate fails (no authorized parties); nomination is not activation; sponsor decision on application
prohibited_outcome: Fund activated with the deceased as advisor or the nominee auto-activated

scenario: Donor signs an amendment replacing the successor two days before death; sponsor countersigns after the death date; family disputes capacity
permitted_outcome: Amendment flagged for review under AUTH-I3; AuthorityState Disputed (CW-30)
prohibited_outcome: Amendment silently effective or silently void

scenario: Sponsor adopts a policy prohibiting a grant category that an accepted field-of-interest restriction requires
permitted_outcome: Review case (AG-05); restriction not overridden by configuration (POL-05)
prohibited_outcome: Policy silently overrides accepted restriction

scenario: Restriction amended (narrowed) after a grant reserved against the restricted balance but before funding
permitted_outcome: Re-check at funding fails; grant held; sponsor decision
prohibited_outcome: Grant funded under the superseded restriction

scenario: Designated fund's sole named beneficiary charity dissolves; agreement names no alternate
permitted_outcome: Variance or redirection workflow with legal review [C] and donor notice
prohibited_outcome: Fund stuck forever because FI-32 blocks every grant; or staff redirect ad hoc
finding_description: No workflow for a restriction or designation that becomes impossible (beneficiary dissolved or ineligible). Accepted donor intent ranks above sponsor policy, so SUCC-06 does not apply. A variance-power style decision path is missing.

scenario: No valid successor; agreement's residual charity has lost exempt status at the time of disposition
permitted_outcome: SUCC-06 sponsor policy determines disposition; eligibility check on the alternate
prohibited_outcome: Grant to the ineligible residual charity

scenario: Check postmarked Dec 31 is received Jan 4; sponsor books it Jan 4
permitted_outcome: Gift-date rule per rail [C] (mailbox rule); acknowledgment date and book date reconciled; Schedule D year defined
prohibited_outcome: Acknowledgment and books disagree with no rule; donor deduction year wrong
finding_description: Completed-gift date is defined only for DTC securities (WF-02). Checks (mailbox rule), ACH and card, crypto confirmations, deed recording and FX wires have no rule. The sponsor's book date and the acknowledgment gift date can diverge, which also shifts the Schedule D year.

scenario: Crypto sent Dec 31 23:50; policy number of confirmations reached Jan 1; processor liquidates Jan 1
permitted_outcome: Gift date by stated rule; acknowledgment in units of the asset (WF-04) with the defined date
prohibited_outcome: Gift date picked per case
finding_description: X-6 for crypto: WF-04 defines settlement by confirmations but not the completed-gift date.

scenario: Custodian DTC receipt file is 3 days late; market rose 6% in between; units have not been issued
permitted_outcome: Stated rule for unit issuance pricing (receipt-date vs recording-date NAV) with no donor option value
prohibited_outcome: Backdated NAV chosen ad hoc; or recording-date pricing applied inconsistently
finding_description: Forward pricing (WF-18 step 3) assumes the receipt is known on the strike day. For late-reported receipts and settlements there is no rule on which NAV applies. FI-28 covers custodian corrections only, not late first reports.

scenario: Liquidation trade for a grant executed Monday; custodian confirmation reported Thursday
permitted_outcome: Pool positions differ from custodian; NAV publication blocked until in-transit item known
prohibited_outcome: NAV published on wrong positions

scenario: Same incoming wire reported by the bank feed and by the custodian cash sweep with different references
permitted_outcome: Single receipt by field-level source of truth; daily legal-owner cash check catches the duplicate
prohibited_outcome: Units and acknowledgment issued twice

scenario: Crypto contribution liquidated and granted; 3 months later analytics re-scores the source wallet as sanctions-linked
permitted_outcome: Sanctions officer case; reporting decision [C]; fund hold; downstream grants reviewed
prohibited_outcome: Silent continuation; or automatic recovery from recipients
finding_description: X-4 on the contribution side: Contribution has Reversed only for rail returns or legal void. There is no post-acceptance tainted or blocked path covering downstream grants or the acknowledgment.

scenario: Accepted LP interest; GP issues a $200k capital call after the advisor's grants consumed the fund's capacity
permitted_outcome: Known unfunded commitments reduce reservable capacity; capital call has a funding source rule
prohibited_outcome: Grants reserve capacity needed for a contractual capital call; fund defaults or goes negative
finding_description: Fund-level obligations that are neither grants nor fees are absent from the twelve financial facts and from C(f,t). This covers capital calls, carrying costs, UBIT (990-T) and transaction or wire charges.

scenario: Real estate held pending sale; property tax, insurance and HOA bills due monthly
permitted_outcome: Defined fund-charge fact with authority, capacity effect and accounting
prohibited_outcome: Paid from sponsor operating cash or fund ad hoc
finding_description: X-8: carrying costs of in-kind assets have no charge type.

scenario: LP interest generated UBTI; sponsor's 990-T tax is allocated after the fund already transferred out
permitted_outcome: Allocation rule and post-closure obligation destination
prohibited_outcome: Tax silently absorbed or charged to unrelated funds
finding_description: X-8: UBIT allocation is undefined. FI-35 covers trailing receipts but not trailing obligations.

scenario: Donor gives 1000 shares and recommends 'grant the proceeds of the sale' to a charity
permitted_outcome: Representable grant type fixed after sale settlement (like FI-15)
prohibited_outcome: Grant fixed at an estimate at approval leaving residual or shortfall
finding_description: FI-16's enumerated denominators exclude a common proceeds-of-contribution grant. FI-15 defines post-settlement fixing only for closing sweeps.

scenario: ACH contribution provisional for 45 days; fees and partner revenue share accrued on it; returned R10
permitted_outcome: Defined fee and partner-share recomputation on reversal (FEE-11 adjustment)
prohibited_outcome: Fees on value that never existed kept by default without a policy
finding_description: FI-22 counts provisional value toward fees. FI-23 does not say whether fees or partner share accrued on reversed value are reversed.

scenario: Contribution under an accepted restriction reverses after restricted grants were paid; the unrestricted balance is positive
permitted_outcome: Restricted sub-balance deficit case and donor receivable; no silent cover from unrestricted
prohibited_outcome: Unrestricted balance silently absorbs the deficit; negative restricted balance hidden

scenario: Donor wires $1,000,000 intending $100,000; asks for the excess back after units and acknowledgment issued
permitted_outcome: Legal determination of gift void for mistake [C]; reversal record if void; acknowledgment corrected
prohibited_outcome: Refund by staff without legal review; or ignore

scenario: Donor dies; monthly ACH contribution pull from donor's account continues for 2 months before notice
permitted_outcome: Standing contribution instructions suspended on death notice; post-death pulls reviewed (estate assets) [C]
prohibited_outcome: Pulls continue after notice; acknowledgments addressed to the deceased
finding_description: CW-11 suspends recurring grant templates but not standing contribution debit authorizations. Treatment of post-death pulls (estate property, acknowledgment addressee) is undefined.

scenario: Another sponsor transfers a donor's fund in by grant, with restrictions and a successor plan; donor asks for a tax acknowledgment
permitted_outcome: Transfer-in classified as a contribution from a public charity; no donor deduction acknowledgment; restrictions and authority established via CW-09
prohibited_outcome: Donor receives a deductible-gift acknowledgment; prior restrictions dropped; prior advisors given authority without agreement
finding_description: Only transfer-out is defined (FI-34). Transfer-in has no classification. Open questions are the contributor party, acknowledgment content, carry-over of restrictions and successor plans, and Schedule D reporting.

scenario: Sponsor converts to a new custodian; positions in transit for 5 days while grants have open liquidation orders
permitted_outcome: Custody-conversion workflow: strike suspension or in-transit accounting, order freeze, truthful grant status
prohibited_outcome: NAV struck on partial positions; orders sent to old custodian
finding_description: No workflow exists for investment-structure transitions (custodian conversion, custodian or processor insolvency, pool merger or liquidation). In-flight orders, unit strike suspension, loss recognition and allocation are undefined.

scenario: Crypto processor freezes withdrawals after receiving a donor's coins but before liquidation; acknowledgment already issued
permitted_outcome: Loss-recognition and allocation decision (fund vs pool vs sponsor); acknowledgment stands as gift completed
prohibited_outcome: Asset carried at pre-failure value; grants funded against it
finding_description: X-13: no rule writes down an asset held at a failed custodian.

scenario: Investment committee merges pool A into pool B on date D; grant redemption orders from A are pending for strikes after D
permitted_outcome: Conversion ratio and order re-routing rule; grant fixed amounts preserved
prohibited_outcome: Orders fail or redeem at an undefined price
finding_description: X-13: FI-33 covers fund merges, not pool reorganizations.

scenario: Percentage grant fixed at approval on a NAV later restated beyond tolerance
permitted_outcome: Grant amount unchanged (single fixing); NAV-error case decides compensation for redeemed units
prohibited_outcome: Grant amount re-fixed; recipient asked to return money

scenario: NAV restated after a fund closed whose residual sweep used the erroneous NAV
permitted_outcome: Fund-level effect computed; compensation routed to residual destination
prohibited_outcome: Fund reopened as Active

scenario: Professional investment advisor terminated for misconduct; still places trades via the custodian trading authorization for 3 days
permitted_outcome: Revocation propagates to external authorizations within a stated window; trades outside authority become an incident
prohibited_outcome: Unbounded window because AUTH-I1 covers only internal sessions and tokens
finding_description: AUTH-I1 invalidates internal sessions, tokens and agent privileges only. Authorizations held at third parties (custodian trading LOAs, bank portal users, payment-provider user lists) have no revocation requirement or staleness window.

scenario: Payment releaser terminated; remains an approver on the bank's manual-wire portal for 10 days
permitted_outcome: Third-party authority lists in the deprovisioning scope with a stated SLA and evidence
prohibited_outcome: Former staff can release wires
finding_description: X-14 for workforce: IAM deprovisioning does not cover external signatory lists.

scenario: Donor recommends moving all units from pool A to B while a percentage grant's funding line draws from A
permitted_outcome: Line becomes a shortfall and is re-planned to other permitted sources; reservation is in currency so unaffected
prohibited_outcome: Grant underfunded or reallocation blocked silently

scenario: Custodian resends a pooled dividend with a new transaction ID in a corrected feed
permitted_outcome: Pool-vs-custodian check fails; break; NAV not published until deduplicated
prohibited_outcome: NAV inflated by double income

scenario: Same custodian historical position correction delivered twice
permitted_outcome: Idempotent bitemporal correction
prohibited_outcome: Correction applied twice and NAV double-adjusted

scenario: Custodian executes a grant liquidation twice; market moves before the reversing trade
permitted_outcome: Trade-error case; error party bears market loss by stated rule
prohibited_outcome: Loss left in the pool by default
finding_description: No inter-fund correction mechanism and no rule on who absorbs operational-error losses (fund, pool or sponsor). CON-3 covers only donor-caused reversals. Cases: misapplied receipts, mis-sourced grants, wrong-recipient re-grants, duplicate trades.

scenario: Court order freezes a fund; quarterly fee accrual date arrives
permitted_outcome: Frozen rule: nothing moves including fees unless legal authority permits [C]
prohibited_outcome: Fee collected from frozen fund by default job

scenario: Foreign grant sent by SHA wire; intermediary bank deducts $35; charity receives less than the fixed amount
permitted_outcome: Charge-bearer rule per grant; either fund bears charges or recipient is told
prohibited_outcome: Recipient silently receives less than approved (prohibited by FI concurrency table)
finding_description: X-8: wire and transaction charges are not a modeled fact, so the GR-1 fixed amount can be violated.

scenario: Payment attempt is Unknown on Dec 31 at year-end close
permitted_outcome: Defined recognition point for grants (approval vs disbursement) [C]; disclosure of unresolved attempts
prohibited_outcome: Grant counted or not counted in Schedule D by implementer choice
finding_description: Recognition of grants and contributions for financial statements and 990/Schedule D is undefined: approval vs disbursement, provisional contributions, Unknown attempts. So is treatment of cross-period returns, voids, reversals and restatements. Only refunds have an owner decision (OD-09).

scenario: Grant paid in December and reported in Schedule D; ACH return arrives January after 990 prepared
permitted_outcome: Stated cross-period rule [C] and current-period entry
prohibited_outcome: Prior-year report silently edited; or return ignored for reporting
finding_description: X-16: returns crossing a filing year.

scenario: Check issued November year 1 voided May year 2 and redirected to a different charity
permitted_outcome: Stated reporting treatment for void and redirect across years
prohibited_outcome: Both grants counted; or neither
finding_description: X-16: voids and reissues crossing a filing year.

scenario: December ACH contribution counted in Schedule D contributions returns in February; acknowledgment issued via the CON-2 correction path
permitted_outcome: Acknowledgment corrected (CON-2) plus a stated Schedule D treatment
prohibited_outcome: Contribution total left overstated with no rule
finding_description: X-16: contribution reversal crossing a filing year. CON-2 covers the acknowledgment but not the sponsor's own reporting.

scenario: Provider certifies NotReceived for an Unknown attempt; a new attempt is sent; next day bank statement shows the first debit
permitted_outcome: Unknown resolves only when provider and bank statement agree, or by human decision with recovery plan
prohibited_outcome: Second attempt allowed on provider proof alone; double payment
finding_description: Conflict: PA-2 allows Unknown to become NotReceived on provider proof alone. Ontology §3 says payment outcome stays Unknown until provider and bank statement agree.

scenario: Payment provider accepts a batch, holds funds, then enters receivership; settlement never occurs
permitted_outcome: Human decision path to treat Accepted as lost with claim against provider, re-pay from a defined source, and record loss bearer
prohibited_outcome: Grant stuck forever because PA-1 forbids a new attempt while Accepted; or silent re-pay
finding_description: The attempt machine has no exit from Accepted when the provider fails. PA-1 then blocks re-payment indefinitely, and nothing says whether the fund or the sponsor bears the loss.

scenario: Return notice webhook arrives before the settlement webhook (out of order)
permitted_outcome: Observation recorded; ordering resolved per INT-05; end state Returned
prohibited_outcome: Return rejected because Accepted to Returned is not a legal transition

scenario: Washed check presented with altered payee and amount; bank pays it
permitted_outcome: Settlement amount mismatch triggers exception; recovery case; bank claim
prohibited_outcome: Treated as normal settlement

scenario: Wrong charity with similar name paid and Final; intended re-grant needs capacity the fund lacks while recovery is pending
permitted_outcome: Recovery case plus new grant; stated rule whether sponsor fronts the amount (sponsor error)
prohibited_outcome: Fund silently negative; or donor bears sponsor's error by default
finding_description: X-15: the compensation rule (recovery plus new grant) does not say who funds the new grant when the error was the sponsor's.

scenario: Advisor with two funds recommends from fund A but meant fund B; paid; asks for reattribution
permitted_outcome: Inter-fund correction record linked to the grant; Schedule D unaffected; audit trail
prohibited_outcome: Paid grant edited to reference fund B
finding_description: X-15: no inter-fund reclass mechanism.

scenario: Custodian credits a stock gift to another fund because of a reference typo; that fund's advisor grants from it before discovery
permitted_outcome: Correction moves units with NAV difference rule; deficit in the wrong fund owned by a stated rule
prohibited_outcome: CON-3 donor receivable applied to an innocent donor; silent negative balance
finding_description: X-15: correcting a misapplied receipt after the wrong fund has spent it.

scenario: Grant returned by charity's bank while the fund has newly become Frozen (donor sanctions listing)
permitted_outcome: Fund re-credited in cash; re-pay held under GR-7 and Frozen
prohibited_outcome: Automatic re-pay to new profile

scenario: Migrated recurring template points to an EIN the incumbent mapped wrongly between two same-name charities
permitted_outcome: Per-instance resolution and eligibility on the exact EIN; ambiguity referred
prohibited_outcome: Payment to wrong organization

scenario: Charity payment-network directory publishes new bank details that differ from the sponsor's verified profile
permitted_outcome: Mismatch forces hold; re-verification through verified channel
prohibited_outcome: Directory value silently replaces profile

scenario: Receiving sponsor of a transfer-out loses public-charity status between approval and wire
permitted_outcome: Release-time re-check holds payment
prohibited_outcome: Transfer wired

scenario: Fund split 60/40 on divorce settlement while one ACH contribution is provisional; it returns after the split
permitted_outcome: Stated lineage rule allocating the reversal and receivable to children
prohibited_outcome: Reversal lands on a closed parent; or both children unaffected
finding_description: After a merge or split, late economic events (returns, refunds, contribution reversals, Unknown attempts resolving, pooled trailing receipts) and non-financial attachments (recurring templates, open flags, holds, successor plans) have no routing rule. FI-33 says only 'explicit rule' for reservations; FI-35 covers closure only.

scenario: Fund A merged into B while an A grant payment is Unknown; it resolves NotReceived and must be re-paid; A's recurring templates also pending
permitted_outcome: Attempt, reservation and templates carried by stated rule; re-pay from successor
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay blocked or from the wrong fund; templates orphaned or active under A's authors without review
finding_description: X-19: in-flight attempts and templates in a merge.

scenario: Transfer-out completed and fund closed; receiving sponsor's bank returns the wire 10 days later
permitted_outcome: Closure waits until Final per rail, or returned cash handled by stated rule (re-pay vs destination)
prohibited_outcome: FI-19 re-credits a closed fund; or FI-35 routes the whole fund balance to the residual destination
finding_description: FUND-1 requires attempts in terminal states, but Settled is not terminal in the attempt machine (Settled to Returned or Voided). Closure therefore never qualifies literally, or proceeds with return risk. Late returns after closure conflict across FI-19, FI-35 and GR Returned to Funded.

scenario: Closure requested; all grants Settled for 30 days; no attempt is in a terminal state
permitted_outcome: Defined closure condition (e.g. grant Final) consistent with attempt states
prohibited_outcome: Closure permanently blocked; or implementer ignores FUND-1
finding_description: X-20: FUND-1 cannot be satisfied as written.

scenario: Class-action proceeds arrive for securities the pool held in 2019; some 2019 unitholders have closed or merged
permitted_outcome: Stated attribution basis (current pool holders vs historical holders) and routing
prohibited_outcome: Ad hoc allocation
finding_description: X-19: FI-35 implies fund-level routing, while pooled receipts flow to current holders through NAV. The basis is unstated.

scenario: Merge proposed where the source fund is Frozen
permitted_outcome: Merge blocked; no automated path out of Frozen
prohibited_outcome: Merge used as a way out of the freeze

scenario: One of two co-advisors in a dispute requests transfer-out to another sponsor
permitted_outcome: Disputed authority holds the request; quorum or all required
prohibited_outcome: Transfer executed on one advisor's request

scenario: Divorce court order directs splitting a joint fund between ex-spouse co-advisors
permitted_outcome: Split via sponsor decision with legal review [C]; conservation by source and restriction
prohibited_outcome: Split executed directly from order without sponsor control analysis

scenario: Wealth-firm distribution partner goes bankrupt; donors only had federated login; accrued revenue share unpaid
permitted_outcome: Partner sessions revoked; donors keep direct access; fee share stops at effective date
prohibited_outcome: Donors locked out; fee share keeps accruing

scenario: Sponsor merges into another sponsoring organization (or its exemption is revoked)
permitted_outcome: Sponsor-succession workflow: agreement novation, acknowledgment issuer entity, custody re-titling, reporting cutoff [C]
prohibited_outcome: Acknowledgments issued by a dissolved entity; funds transferred without legal review
finding_description: The ontology lists sponsor states dissolved/merged but no workflow covers sponsor or legal-entity succession. Missing: agreement novation, acknowledgment issuer, Schedule D cutoff, custody re-titling.

scenario: Pricing vendor outage leaves no NAV for 3 days during year-end percentage grants
permitted_outcome: Latest struck NAV with as-of or defer fixing
prohibited_outcome: Fabricated value

scenario: Provisional credit limit lowered while existing reservations rely on provisional value under the old limit
permitted_outcome: Existing reservations stand (checked at creation); new ones under new limit
prohibited_outcome: Retroactive release of reservations

scenario: Haircut rates raised during market stress; many funds become over-committed
permitted_outcome: New reservations refused; approved grants keep fixed amounts; cases
prohibited_outcome: Approved grants silently reduced

scenario: New inactivity policy triggers sponsor disposition for legacy-agreement funds with no inactivity clause
permitted_outcome: No retroactive application without approved transition; agreement conflict review
prohibited_outcome: Policy applied silently to legacy funds

scenario: Board amends gift-acceptance delegation while a complex asset accepted under the old delegation is in TransferInProgress
permitted_outcome: Decision made under authority at the time stands; dependent policies suspended and re-linked
prohibited_outcome: Accepted gift reversed; or new acceptances under lapsed delegation

scenario: Successor activated; later a valid amendment naming a different successor surfaces; activated successor's grants already paid
permitted_outcome: Revoke and replace; past grants flagged for review (effective-in-past analogue)
prohibited_outcome: Paid grants unwound automatically

scenario: Disputant submits through a partner widget whose launch grant has not been invalidated after Disputed status
permitted_outcome: Command re-checked; held
prohibited_outcome: Accepted under stale widget authority

scenario: One co-donor of a joint fund is SDN-listed
permitted_outcome: Fund Frozen; all grants held; reporting
prohibited_outcome: Grants continue

scenario: Compromised partner page uses navigationRequested to open a lookalike 'sponsor re-login' top-level page, harvests the donor's TOTP and then recommends a grant to a new charity it controls
permitted_outcome: Reauth only on sponsor origin; phishable session cannot auto-approve a new recipient; hold pending phishing-resistant step-up
prohibited_outcome: Harvested TOTP session auto-approves and pays a new recipient

scenario: Host sizes the iframe so the review panel (recipient, amount, disclaimer) is clipped while the Submit control stays visible
permitted_outcome: Widget withholds Submit unless the review content is rendered at manifest MinWidth; otherwise top-level handoff
prohibited_outcome: Submission of an effect the user never saw
governing_rules: W01 manifest MinWidth; WG-4; GRW-11; GRW-15

scenario: Host fabricates 'Grant approved and sent' copy from an opaque commandAccepted event; sponsor later declines; donor relies on host copy for tax planning
permitted_outcome: Host copy limited to 'recommendation submitted'; donor sees authoritative status sponsor-direct
prohibited_outcome: Host statement treated as sponsor record or as payment
governing_rules: TVR-WID-005; widget consistency rules 1 and 3; GRW-12

scenario: Partner admin uses self-service to add a staging origin on a shared multi-tenant hosting domain to ApprovedOrigins
permitted_outcome: Security review; exact non-shared origins only; change audited
prohibited_outcome: Widget frameable from any tenant of the shared host
governing_rules: W01 trust item 5; W01 governance (self-service cannot add unrestricted origins); P19

scenario: WG-4 visibility check false-positives for a screen-magnifier user at 400% zoom and blocks Submit with no alternative
permitted_outcome: Accessible top-level handoff on sponsor origin
prohibited_outcome: Lockout that pushes the donor into an uncontrolled assisted channel

scenario: Advisor host page shows two widget instances for two client funds side by side; advisor drafts in fund A believing it is fund B
permitted_outcome: Each instance shows trusted sponsor and fund identity; review names fund; drafts isolated
prohibited_outcome: Ambiguous context leads to grant from wrong client fund
governing_rules: GRW-16; GRW-18; P5 context indicator; W01 trust item 9

scenario: Partner IdP reassigns a departed advisor's email/sub to a new hire; launch maps the new hire to the old advisor's PrivilegeGrants on 40 donor funds
permitted_outcome: Mapping keyed on immutable iss+sub plus SCIM externalId; reuse detected; new subject has no privileges until donor consents
prohibited_outcome: New hire inherits view and recommend rights
governing_rules: Widget trace step 1 (mapping audited); identity principle 5
finding_description: Subject-mapping integrity is unspecified: mapping changes are only 'audited events'. No rule forbids identifier recycling (email/sub reuse), requires dual control or donor notice for mapping changes, or binds mapping to immutable iss+sub/externalId.

scenario: Partner admin colludes with a sponsor onboarding staffer to remap a partner user to a wealthy donor's party
permitted_outcome: Sponsor-side mapping change needs dual control and notice to the donor via a sponsor-direct channel
prohibited_outcome: Single staffer remaps subject; access granted silently
finding_description: Same gap as S-8: a sponsor-side mapping change is in effect an authority change but is not in the authority-transition table (org §5.3) and has no dual control or donor notice.

scenario: Partner offboarded; 12,000 donors only ever authenticated through the partner IdP and hold no sponsor credential; help desk runs mass re-proofing
permitted_outcome: Pre-registered sponsor-direct factor, or governed re-proofing with CTL-054 cooling-off; status readable during transition
prohibited_outcome: Mass help-desk recovery without cooling-off, or donors locked out of their funds
governing_rules: Widget consistency rule 3; org §5.3 partner offboarded; CTL-054
finding_description: Rule 3 promises a sponsor-direct channel, but no requirement gives partner-federated donors a sponsor credential before partner exit. Exit becomes a mass-recovery event (the weakest link) or a lockout. Advisor firm moves have no donor-consented re-association path.

scenario: Advisor moves from Partner A to Partner B; Partner B requests launches for the same donors citing the advisor's relationship
permitted_outcome: Cross-organization access denied until the donor grants a new privilege in their own session
prohibited_outcome: Partner B gains access on advisor assertion

scenario: Partner terminated but its mTLS machine clients and webhook subscriptions stay registered; partner CRM keeps pulling positions
permitted_outcome: Registration status Terminated blocks all clients, tokens and webhooks at effective time
prohibited_outcome: Continued data flow after offboarding
governing_rules: Org §5.3 partner offboarded; TVR-WID-003; CTL-034; CTL-053

scenario: Partner quietly downgrades to SMS OTP but keeps asserting amr=mfa under its existing MFA attestation
permitted_outcome: AAL2-only effect (routine); phishing-resistant actions still need hwk/phr or local step-up; periodic re-attestation
prohibited_outcome: Partner downgrade lets SMS sessions perform sensitive actions

scenario: Compromised partner backend uses the headless API (recommendations:write) and a partner-hosted CIBA confirmation to submit and self-confirm grants to new recipients for hundreds of donors
permitted_outcome: Confirmation for new recipients or high value goes through a sponsor-direct channel independent of the partner; fan-out caps hold excess
prohibited_outcome: Partner-controlled confirmation counted as donor confirmation
governing_rules: Identity principle 8 (RAR/CIBA via partner); TVR-WID-004 (widgets only); CTL-029
finding_description: TVR-WID-004 requires sponsor-verified step-up only for transactional widgets. The headless API (M2) and partner-offered CIBA keep confirmation inside the partner's trust boundary, so a compromised partner can both request and confirm. Requirement: a channel-independent rule that new-recipient or above-threshold confirmation is sponsor-direct.

scenario: Partner IdP signing key stolen; attacker forges fresh amr=hwk assertions for mapped donors and recommends $40k to a new charity via widget
permitted_outcome: Sponsor-verified step-up for new recipient (TVR-WID-004); velocity caps; hold
prohibited_outcome: Forged partner amr satisfies phishing-resistant requirement

scenario: Partner SCIM endpoint fails for 3 days; leavers keep federated access
permitted_outcome: CTL-052 latency monitor alerts; contractual maximum; sponsor revokes sessions independently
prohibited_outcome: Indefinite access by former partner staff

scenario: Partner suspended in December over a fee dispute while thousands of donors have drafts and submitted recommendations
permitted_outcome: Submitted recommendations proceed; new commands blocked; donors told via sponsor channel
prohibited_outcome: Submitted recommendations dropped

scenario: Charity changes bank details through sponsor A's process on the shared verified payee registry (AO-07); sponsor B pays the new account without its own cooling-off or out-of-band check
permitted_outcome: Each tenant applies its own payee controls, or relies only on a registry-level control at least as strict as every tenant's policy, with provenance
prohibited_outcome: One tenant's weaker or compromised verification changes another tenant's payment destination
finding_description: Multi-sponsor isolation is stated only as per-tenant cells and keys (DD-016; security §3). Shared cross-tenant services (verified payee registry AO-07, verification network AO-02, customer identity, partner registrations, agent corpora) have no rule preventing one tenant's change or verification from becoming another tenant's decision input. allowed(command) in org §5.2 has no explicit tenant/legal-entity term.

scenario: Migration import produces colliding fund identifiers; a read-model cache keyed without tenant shows sponsor A data to a sponsor B user
permitted_outcome: Tenant in every key and authorization; per-tenant cells; typed opaque IDs
prohibited_outcome: Cross-tenant data disclosure
governing_rules: DD-016 cells; W01 manifest (never infer tenant from display identifier); security §3 per-tenant keys

scenario: Same person donates at sponsors A and B on a shared customer identity platform; help-desk recovery at A (looser policy) yields a session that B accepts
permitted_outcome: Recovery and assurance evaluated per tenant; a recovery event in one tenant triggers cooling-off in all
prohibited_outcome: Cross-tenant session acceptance after one tenant's recovery
finding_description: Shared identity across sponsors is not addressed. Recovery, assurance and cooling-off are defined per platform, not per tenant (S-3).

scenario: AG-13 policy drafting and AG-16 improvement receive pooled cross-sponsor corpora; sponsor A's draft reveals sponsor B's thresholds and donor patterns
permitted_outcome: Corpora and agent contexts scoped per tenant unless contractually pooled with de-identification
prohibited_outcome: Cross-tenant leakage through model context
finding_description: Pseudonymization and aggregation rules set no tenant boundary for agent inputs (S-3).

scenario: Under Model C an operator SRE, JIT-approved by an operator manager, corrects sponsor A's grant record; sponsor A's board never delegated authority to operator staff
