permitted_outcome: Operator staff act only under a sponsor DoA or a sponsor-approved JIT; the sponsor sees and approves operator access
prohibited_outcome: Operator workforce changes sponsor records outside the sponsor's exclusive legal control
governing_rules: Org §5.1 workforce role; CTL-031; DD-016; REG-001
finding_description: The authority model assumes workforce = sponsor staff. Under Models B/C the operator's staff are not covered by the sponsor's DoA, and the operator approves JIT itself. Requirement: operator access to tenant records needs a sponsor-side approver and a DoA link, and the sponsor receives the access log.

scenario: Enterprise payments pause triggered for a sponsor A incident halts sponsor B's year-end grants on the same platform
permitted_outcome: Kill switches scoped by tenant, partner, channel and agent; cross-tenant pause only for a platform-level incident, with notice
prohibited_outcome: Blast radius set by the switch design rather than by the incident
finding_description: CTL-028 defines only per-agent and enterprise pause. Scope (tenant/partner/channel), independence from a compromised control plane, and resume preconditions are unspecified. Payments-pause release is dual control (K §12) but nothing requires a review of changes made during the incident window.

scenario: Partner contracted with sponsors A and B requests a launch for a fund at A for a subject whose relationship exists only at B
permitted_outcome: Launch denied (ScopeDenied)
prohibited_outcome: Cross-sponsor launch

scenario: Launch artifact leaks through partner server access logs; attacker exchanges it before the user's browser does
permitted_outcome: Single use; the legitimate exchange gets ReplayRejected and raises a security event; short TTL; bound to origin and nonce
prohibited_outcome: Silent shared session

scenario: Attacker hijacks a donor session minutes after the donor completed passkey step-up for a $30k grant and, inside the 15-minute freshness window, submits $30k to a new recipient
permitted_outcome: Step-up for a new recipient or high value is bound to that transaction's canonical payload
prohibited_outcome: Time-window freshness authorizes an unrelated transaction
governing_rules: DD-021 action table (15 min freshness); TVCTL-06
finding_description: Sensitive-action assurance is time-window based (fresh within 15 min). Nothing binds the step-up or confirmation to the specific recipient and amount. Requirement: transaction-bound confirmation (sponsor-rendered payload hash in the WebAuthn challenge or RAR) for new recipients and above-threshold grants.

scenario: Captured SubmitGrantRecommendation replayed with the same idempotency key but a changed amount
permitted_outcome: Request-hash mismatch rejected; original receipt returned only for an identical request
prohibited_outcome: Second or altered recommendation

scenario: Old signed provider Returned webhook replayed to re-credit a fund a second time
permitted_outcome: Idempotent observation by provider event ID
prohibited_outcome: Double re-credit

scenario: Donor agent's DPoP key is software-held and is exfiltrated together with its token
permitted_outcome: Revocation; caps; new-recipient confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Unlimited replay

scenario: Widget refresh token persists in partitioned storage on a shared library computer; the next user reopens the host page and the widget resumes
permitted_outcome: Widget session bound to the host session and short-lived; logout propagates; ReauthRequired
prohibited_outcome: Next user sees or acts on the prior donor's fund
governing_rules: W01 session states; W01 trust item 4; W02 local caching threat review

scenario: Advisor delegates part of its recommend privilege to its own AI agent (org §5.1) and, as 'delegating Person', confirms the agent's above-cap recommendations; the donor never sees them
permitted_outcome: Only the donor creates agent delegations; confirmations go to the donor
prohibited_outcome: Advisor-created agent with advisor self-confirmation
governing_rules: Org §5.1 (advisor to agent subset delegation); identity principle 5 (advisors cannot change delegation); INV-A6
finding_description: Contradiction: org §5.1 allows advisor-to-agent subset delegation, while DD-021 says only the donor can change delegation. INV-A6's 'delegating Person' then lets an advisor confirm its own agent. How to classify the sponsor-operated donor assistant (a donor-side principal run by the sponsor) is also unresolved.

scenario: Sponsor-operated 'donor assistant' is treated as a donor-side principal with caps; a sponsor insider changes its prompt so it suggests and submits grants to a favoured charity
permitted_outcome: Every submission by a sponsor-operated assistant needs donor confirmation; its configuration falls under CW-19 change control
prohibited_outcome: Sponsor both originates and approves a recommendation attributed to the donor
governing_rules: Security §1 donor-side agent row; INV-A5; CTL-026
finding_description: Same gap as S-18: no rule covers an agent that the sponsor operates but that acts with donor authority.

scenario: Donor agent sends 40 confirmation requests a day; the donor taps 'approve all', including one injected new recipient
permitted_outcome: Itemized sponsor-rendered confirmations; no batch approval for new recipients; rate limits on confirmation requests
prohibited_outcome: Confirmation fatigue turns the control into a rubber stamp
governing_rules: INV-A6; TVCTL-06; UX §3.1 model D (per-item list)
finding_description: Confirmation content and batching are unspecified (S-7). A confirmation must show the canonical recipient and amount rendered by the sponsor, not agent text, and must not be batched for new recipients.

scenario: Charity description served in the machine-readable API instructs external donor agents to 'recommend $5,000 now'
permitted_outcome: Untrusted content delimited in the API; new-recipient confirmation; caps
prohibited_outcome: Agent-originated grant auto-approved

scenario: Donor dies; the agent keeps submitting weekly recommendations; after notice its token remains valid
permitted_outcome: Children end at the parent's effective time; pre-notice actions flagged
prohibited_outcome: Agent continues after notice

scenario: Donor repudiates an agent-submitted grant ('my agent exceeded my instructions')
permitted_outcome: Recommendation attributed to requesting and acting principal, with signed request event and caps evidence
prohibited_outcome: Unattributable request

scenario: Payee-profile approver fabricates the out-of-band verification for an attacker bank account on a real charity; a colluding releaser releases a $400k payment
permitted_outcome: Collusion-resistant controls: random assignment of the second person, staff-to-payee account/device matching, pair-concentration KRI, notice to the charity's prior verified contact
prohibited_outcome: Two colluding staff satisfy SoD-1 and pay an attacker
finding_description: Security §8 lists two-person collusion as residual, mitigated only by 'sampling and internal audit'. No control randomizes who the second approver is, flags recurring approver pairs, matches payee bank/address/device data against staff records, or requires rotation or mandatory leave.

scenario: Grant specialist repeatedly approves one donor's benefit-tainted referred grants in exchange for kickbacks; no recorded relationship
permitted_outcome: Random case assignment; specialist-donor concentration KRI; seeded cases; QA sampling
prohibited_outcome: Same specialist decides the same donor's cases indefinitely
finding_description: Same gap as S-1: case routing does not stop a reviewer from repeatedly receiving or picking one requester, and no KRI watches reviewer-requester concentration.

scenario: Policy author and publisher collude to loosen fuzzy-match sensitivity, labelling the change a tightening
permitted_outcome: Automated monotonic classification forces Change Board and CRCO; back-test shows the loosening
prohibited_outcome: Loosening published by two people

scenario: Payment releaser and the independent reconciler collude to clear the break for a misdirected payment
permitted_outcome: External auditor verification; write-off second approver; break aging escalation
prohibited_outcome: Break cleared and concealed
finding_description: TVCTL-07 makes reconciliation independent, but two-person collusion still defeats it (S-1). There is no pair KRI and no rotation requirement.

scenario: Engineer with JIT production write access edits a verified payee profile's bank token in the database while working a ticket
permitted_outcome: JIT scopes exclude payee, ledger and authority tables; any authoritative row change without a causing command is detected before payment
prohibited_outcome: Payment gate pays a hijacked but 'verified' profile
finding_description: CTL-031 says JIT exists, not what JIT may write. Direct data edits bypass CTL-004 and SM-1 because no command occurs. Requirement: no human write path to payee, authority, ledger or policy stores except domain commands; a continuous integrity check that every authoritative state change has a matching command event; and the payment gate refuses profiles whose state hash disagrees.

scenario: Break-glass account used at 03:00 to set a fund's AuthorityState and activate a successor; review is weekly
permitted_outcome: Break-glass cannot perform domain transitions; any use pages the CISO and holds affected subjects pending review
prohibited_outcome: Authority changed via break-glass and acted on before review
finding_description: Break-glass is 'sealed, alarmed and reviewed', but its permitted actions and a hold on affected subjects are not defined (S-9).

scenario: Data scientist relabels a real fraudulent referred grant as a CTL-046 seeded case so it is excluded from metrics and investigation
permitted_outcome: Seeded-case register held by internal audit, sealed and write-once; operators cannot label
prohibited_outcome: Real case hidden as a test
finding_description: Seeded cases (CTL-046) and canary grants (TVCTL-04) live in production, with no rule on who registers them, how they are kept out of financial and regulatory populations, or how a real item is protected from relabelling.

scenario: Engineer and a colluding code reviewer merge a payment-gate change that skips cooling-off for one payee flag
permitted_outcome: Change Board approval for control-touching deploys; production invariant tests on CTL-003
prohibited_outcome: Control bypass shipped by two developers

scenario: Grant approver pressures the sanctions officer to clear a true match on the same case
permitted_outcome: Sanctions officer clears only with evidence; approver is not the sanctions officer; flag never expires; escalation to GC
prohibited_outcome: Cleared to meet an SLA

scenario: Caller impersonating an elderly donor (P2) asks support to submit a $20k grant to a new charity by phone; staff enter it in the back office
permitted_outcome: Assisted-channel recommendation has a defined assurance (knowledge-based = AAL1), is attributed to staff plus donor, and a new recipient needs sponsor-direct confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Staff-entered request treated as donor-authenticated and auto-approved
finding_description: The UX requires a phone/human channel for P2/P4, but no requirement defines the assurance level of staff-entered (assisted) recommendations or profile changes, how they are attributed, or their limits. Social engineering of support becomes the cheapest account-takeover path.

scenario: Support agent uses 'view as donor' to troubleshoot and clicks Submit on the donor's draft
permitted_outcome: Support views are read-only; any donor-side command from staff is a distinct assisted command with evidence of the donor's instruction
prohibited_outcome: Command recorded as the donor's own
finding_description: Same gap as S-2: impersonation and view-as modes are not constrained.

scenario: Support JIT access to the identity vault for one case is used to download 500 ID images
permitted_outcome: JIT case-scoped and rate-limited; privileged-session detection in SIEM; review
prohibited_outcome: Bulk export unnoticed
governing_rules: CTL-031; AUTH-10; security §4 identity vault; security §5 SIEM

scenario: SIM-swapped attacker passes help-desk recovery; the prior-channel notice goes to the hijacked phone
permitted_outcome: Cooling-off before payout-relevant actions; notice to all prior channels including email
prohibited_outcome: Immediate grant rights after recovery

scenario: AG-04 dossier cites 'IRS determination letter p.2 confirms public charity status' but the snapshot says private foundation; the specialist relies on the citation
permitted_outcome: Citations mechanically verified against the cited snapshot before display; unverified claims marked
prohibited_outcome: Hallucinated citation drives an approval
finding_description: Grounding checks (CTL-039) apply only to the donor-facing service agent. Staff- and board-facing outputs (AG-03, AG-04, AG-07, AG-18, AG-19) have no citation-fidelity check, yet they feed human decisions.

scenario: AG-19 board narrator misstates the fallback rate and exception backlog in the board pack used to renew the routine-approval delegation
permitted_outcome: Figures in board drafts tied to approved snapshot fields and verified
prohibited_outcome: Board renews the delegation on invented figures
finding_description: Same gap as S-11.

scenario: Model provider silently updates the model behind the same alias; AG-02, AG-03 and AG-17 false negatives rise together and the falling flag rate is masked by the December surge
permitted_outcome: Pinned immutable model snapshots; provider change detected; continuous known-answer canaries per agent
prohibited_outcome: Correlated silent loss of protective flags
finding_description: A model change counts as a version change (security §9.3), but nothing pins immutable snapshots or detects a provider-side change under the same name. Agents sharing one model fail together, and flag-rate drift detection can be hidden by volume. Requirement: pinning, continuous canary sets and a correlation analysis across agents.

scenario: AG-04 summary and AG-02 flag come from the same base model; the reviewer treats their agreement as independent corroboration
permitted_outcome: Shared-model provenance shown; same-model outputs not counted as independent evidence
prohibited_outcome: Correlated AI outputs presented as two lines of defence
finding_description: Same gap as S-10: there is no independence rule for AI outputs that share a model.

scenario: Insider edits the AG-02 system prompt and retrieval exclusions in a config repository; this is not treated as a model or permission change
permitted_outcome: Prompts, retrieval sources and thresholds are versioned agent configuration under CTL-026 and SoD-8
prohibited_outcome: Silent behaviour change suppresses benefit flags
finding_description: CTL-026 gates versions and permission expansions; security §9.3 names model and provider changes. Prompt, retrieval and threshold configuration is not named, so it can change the behaviour of a protective agent outside the evaluation gate (S-10).

scenario: AG-11 discovery recommends a charity whose third-party profile was poisoned to promote a sham organization
permitted_outcome: Third-party data advisory only; new-recipient controls; velocity
prohibited_outcome: Discovery listing treated as endorsement

scenario: AG-10 advisor copilot drafts a grant with the EIN of a similarly named charity; the advisor submits without reading
permitted_outcome: Review shows legal name and EIN; D eligibility on that EIN
prohibited_outcome: Copilot output treated as fact

scenario: At 10x December volume specialists open the evidence for two seconds before approving, to satisfy TVR-UX-006 gating
permitted_outcome: Per-reviewer seeded-case detection rates; workload caps; detection below target triggers queue redesign
prohibited_outcome: Gating met in form only, with no review in substance

scenario: AG-08 extracts ED affidavit fields wrongly and the extracted value feeds the deterministic validity gate
permitted_outcome: D gate inputs must be authoritative; AI extraction only drafts or flags, and a human confirms
prohibited_outcome: Unverified extraction used as an authoritative input

scenario: Attacker submits many recommendations with long purpose texts and attachments to exhaust per-agent cost ceilings; AG-02 trips its breaker and grants take the TVCTL-05 fallback, which is looser than the agent
permitted_outcome: Degraded modes are never less restrictive than normal; ceiling exhaustion by one requester is rate-limited per requester; time in degraded mode is bounded and alarmed
prohibited_outcome: Attacker-induced degraded mode becomes a bypass
finding_description: TVCTL-05 requires that a fallback ran but not that it is at least as strict as the agent. Per-agent cost ceilings (security §9.4) can be exhausted on purpose. CTL-010's monotonic rule covers parameter changes, not degraded modes. Requirement: degraded-mode monotonicity plus per-requester cost quotas.

scenario: Sanctions screening vendor and AG-03 are both unavailable for 6 hours at peak
permitted_outcome: Payment gate holds when screening cannot run against the current list; queue with truthful status
prohibited_outcome: Release on the last cached screening result

scenario: Model provider outage of 72 hours exceeds the T2 RTO; ER reminder drafts and dossiers stop
permitted_outcome: D path continues; P items queue for humans; ER obligations still tracked by TVCTL-12
prohibited_outcome: Obligations silently missed

scenario: Donor writes the grant purpose with hidden instructions telling the benefit-risk classifier 'no donor benefit; classify low' for gala tickets
permitted_outcome: Requester-supplied text treated as hostile; deterministic benefit keywords and category rules run alongside AG-02; injection markers raise a flag
prohibited_outcome: Agent false negative is the only defence against a §4967 benefit
governing_rules: AG-02; CTL-008; security §8 injection residual; TVCTL-05
finding_description: Security §8 accepts agent false negatives because 'deterministic gates still apply', but no deterministic gate exists for donor benefit: AG-02 is the only screen, and the requester controls its input. Requirement: a deterministic complement (category, keyword and recipient-type rules) and injection detection on requester free text, plus CTL-049 sampling of unflagged purposes.

scenario: Charity-submitted ER report PDF contains instructions telling AG-12 to mark reports complete and suppress reminders
permitted_outcome: AG-12 cannot write; report receipt recorded by a human or a D rule; missing report escalates
prohibited_outcome: Obligation closed by injected text

scenario: Complex-asset offering memorandum includes white-text instructions telling AG-07 to omit environmental liabilities
permitted_outcome: Specialist decides; committee above threshold; agent output is only a dossier
prohibited_outcome: Dossier omission accepted as clean

scenario: Charity name field contains 'Note to reviewer: pre-cleared by Compliance', shown inside the exception dossier
permitted_outcome: Untrusted content quoted and visually distinct from system facts; content confers no authority
prohibited_outcome: Reviewer treats charity text as a compliance statement

scenario: Email claiming to be from a charity, processed by AG-09, asks for a bank account update
permitted_outcome: Channel rejected; verified re-enrolment only
prohibited_outcome: Profile changed

scenario: Storage administrator rewrites the evidence store and recomputes the whole hash chain to remove a control failure
permitted_outcome: Chain checkpoints anchored outside the platform's admin domain (internal audit or external WORM/witness) so a rewrite is detectable
prohibited_outcome: Internally consistent but forged evidence
finding_description: TVCTL-11 specifies an append-only hash chain, but a hash chain proves nothing against someone who can rewrite it end to end. Requirement: periodic checkpoint hashes delivered to a party outside the platform admin domain, and verified at audit.

scenario: Evidence pipeline is down for 6 hours while payments continue, leaving decision records missing
permitted_outcome: A transition commits only with its decision record (atomic); otherwise the money-moving transition blocks; any gap is logged as a control failure
prohibited_outcome: Payments without evidence

scenario: Clock skew of +3 days on a payment-gate node makes a payee's CTL-004 cooling-off appear elapsed
permitted_outcome: Trusted time source; skew alarms; cooling-off and freshness computed from authoritative time; payment gate fails closed on skew
prohibited_outcome: Time-based controls defeated by a wrong clock
finding_description: Many controls are time-based (cooling-off, 15-minute freshness, effective-time authority, return windows, data freshness SLOs), but no requirement names an authoritative time source, a skew tolerance or fail-closed behaviour.

scenario: TVCTL-04 canary grants and CTL-046 seeded cases appear in the auditor's sample population and in 990 Schedule D grant counts
permitted_outcome: Seeded items registered, excluded from financial and regulatory populations by a controlled join, and never move real money
prohibited_outcome: Regulatory filings or audit samples contaminated by test items
finding_description: Same gap as S-15: there is no population-exclusion rule for seeded items.

scenario: Point-in-time restore: T1 grant decisioning (RPO 15 min) and T0 payment gate (RPO 5 min) restore to different points, leaving PaymentInstructed without GrantApproved
permitted_outcome: Consistent cross-tier restore point, or decision records in the same tier as payments; post-restore invariant check before resuming
prohibited_outcome: INV-A3 violated after restore; payments with no approval record
finding_description: DR tiers put the payment gate (T0) and grant decisioning (T1) at different RPOs and assign no tier to the evidence store. A restore can break INV-A3 and TVCTL-11. Requirement: one restore-consistency group for decision, payment and evidence records, and an invariant suite that must pass before payments resume.

scenario: Payment gate restored to 5 minutes earlier loses two attempts the provider already Accepted; the grants look Funded with no attempt; ops create new attempts
permitted_outcome: Attempt creation durable with RPO 0 before submission, or mandatory provider reconciliation of the RPO window before any new attempt
prohibited_outcome: Double payment after restore
governing_rules: PA-1; PA-3; TVCTL-02; security §7 RPO 5 min
finding_description: PA-1 assumes local attempt state is complete. With a 5-minute RPO, attempts can vanish locally while live at the provider. TVS-076 covered failover with durable state, not a lossy restore. Requirement: RPO 0 for attempt records, or a blocking provider-side reconciliation of the RPO window.

scenario: Ransomware encrypts the primary systems and online backups
permitted_outcome: Immutable or offline backups; cold-standby restore tested; payments paused until invariants are verified
prohibited_outcome: Restore from a tampered backup; unknown payment state

scenario: Workforce identity platform compromised; the kill-switch console uses the same SSO and attackers lock responders out
permitted_outcome: Kill switch operable through an out-of-band path independent of the compromised IdP, with sealed credentials and two-person activation
prohibited_outcome: Responders unable to pause payments during an active attack
finding_description: Same gap as S-16: the kill switch's independence from the compromised plane is not required.

scenario: After a 2-day payments pause for a payee-hijack incident, dual control releases the pause; queued payments include profiles, delegations and recovery factors changed during the incident window
permitted_outcome: Resume requires a review and re-verification of every payee, delegation and recovery change made in the window
prohibited_outcome: Bulk release of payments to profiles altered by the attacker
governing_rules: CTL-028; K §12 pause release dual control; SM-6; CTL-004
finding_description: Same gap as S-16: SM-6 re-checks status at release but does not re-verify profiles marked verified during the compromise.

scenario: Defective AG-17 version raises 20,000 false related-party flags in December; INV-A4 blocks approvals; staff propose a database bulk clear
permitted_outcome: Governed class-level supersession: a named person decides for the defective version's flags, with sampling and a record; no direct data edit
prohibited_outcome: Ad hoc bulk clear, or year-end stall
finding_description: Class-level (bulk) decisions are unspecified. Flags from a quarantined agent version need a governed supersession path, or staff will improvise (S-19).

scenario: Provider degradation at 10x volume leaves 4,000 Unknown attempts; ops propose a bulk 'NotReceived' to meet year-end
permitted_outcome: Unknown resolves per attempt on provider evidence, or through a provider-attested batch reconciliation file; bulk human resolution prohibited
prohibited_outcome: Mass duplicate payments
finding_description: PA-2 and TVCTL-02 define one decision with two approvers, but nothing prohibits a class-level PA-2 decision under volume pressure, and there is no provider-side batch-proof path. Requirement: bulk Unknown resolution only on provider-attested evidence per attempt.

scenario: Partner compromise discovered; the sponsor must list every recommendation made through that partner's integration during the window
permitted_outcome: Token-exchange actor and partner client recorded on each command; query by partner and time
prohibited_outcome: Cannot scope the incident

scenario: 10x December surge trips enterprise-window fan-out caps for legitimate grants; ops raise the caps under pressure
permitted_outcome: Raising caps is a loosening (Change Board plus CRCO); seasonal parameters pre-approved with expiry
prohibited_outcome: Caps raised informally mid-surge

scenario: A sanctions list update during a 10x surge needs a full rescreen; payments are submitted before the rescreen finishes on the new list
permitted_outcome: Payment gate re-checks against the current list version at submission; data-freshness block
prohibited_outcome: Release screened only against the superseded list

scenario: Screen-reader user approves a CIBA/push confirmation whose OS notification truncates the recipient and amount
permitted_outcome: Confirmation content fully perceivable through AT (sponsor page, not truncated OS text); accessible alternative before approval
prohibited_outcome: User confirms a transaction they could not perceive
finding_description: UXA-3 covers an accessible authentication method, not accessible presentation of what is being confirmed. Out-of-band confirmations and regenerated previews have no requirement that the transaction details are perceivable, and that changes are announced, before consent.

scenario: Preview expires during a slow assistive-technology review; the regenerated preview changes a percentage-derived amount from $9,800 to $9,200 without announcement; the user submits
permitted_outcome: Material change between previews highlighted and announced; renewed explicit review
prohibited_outcome: Submission on a superseded mental model
finding_description: Same gap as S-17: UXA-4 restores the draft but does not require that preview changes be announced.

scenario: User with a comma-decimal locale types '1.000' meaning one thousand and it is parsed as $1.00; another types '5,000' meaning five and gets $5,000
permitted_outcome: Locale-explicit parsing; review states the amount in currency and words; large-change warning
prohibited_outcome: Silent mis-scaled amount

scenario: Charity combobox selects on arrow focus; a screen-reader user tabs away leaving an adjacent similarly named charity selected
permitted_outcome: Explicit activation; review reads legal name, city and EIN in order
prohibited_outcome: Wrong recipient chosen silently

scenario: State AG subpoena requires partner-side launch and event logs; the partner was offboarded and has already given a deletion attestation (WG-7)
permitted_outcome: Deletion obligations subordinate to legal-hold notices; partner contract includes preservation on notice
prohibited_outcome: Evidence destroyed under a sponsor-mandated deletion
finding_description: WG-7 requires partners to delete received data on exit, with no carve-out for legal holds or regulatory inquiries.

scenario: SOC 1 auditor requests the population of routine D approvals in a period, each with its linked board delegation
permitted_outcome: Per-decision policy-version and delegation link; population with numerator, denominator and status
prohibited_outcome: Population drawn from a projection without provenance

scenario: IRS examiner asks why a D-path grant was approved two years ago
permitted_outcome: Decision record with policy version, input snapshot hash and eligibility data version
prohibited_outcome: Reconstruction from current data

scenario: External auditor's read-only account (P15) is phished and used to export full populations
permitted_outcome: Scoped, time-bound auditor access with phishing-resistant MFA; no identity-vault access; export volume alerts
prohibited_outcome: Auditor account becomes a bulk exfiltration path

scenario: In a dispute, a regulator asks what the donor was shown (available estimate and disclaimers) when submitting
permitted_outcome: GrantPreview content and hash retained with the submission
prohibited_outcome: Cannot prove what was displayed

scenario: Split disbursement under per-payment rail cap: tranche 1 ($1M) Settled; tranche 2 ($1M) Failed; no live attempt remains
permitted_outcome: Grant shows part-paid; sponsor creates tranche-2 retry or cancels the unpaid remainder with reservation partly released
prohibited_outcome: Grant stuck in Disbursing; or moved to Funded as if nothing settled; or shown 'Paid'
finding_description: Rev 2 PA-1 permits split disbursement but the grant machine was not updated: Disbursing->Funded requires all attempts terminal WITHOUT settlement and Disbursing->Disbursed requires cumulative settled = amount, so a grant with one tranche Settled and the rest Failed/Voided has no exit; there is no Disbursing->Disbursing edge for the next tranche, no edge for a return of one tranche, and no headline or date rule for part-paid grants.

scenario: Split grant fully Disbursed; tranche 1 of 2 returned R03 while tranche 2 is Final
permitted_outcome: Grant returns to a part-paid state; only returned amount re-reserved; headline shows part paid / returned
prohibited_outcome: Whole grant shown Returned; or both tranches re-paid
finding_description: Rev 2 PA-1 permits split disbursement but the grant machine was not updated: Disbursing->Funded requires all attempts terminal WITHOUT settlement and Disbursing->Disbursed requires cumulative settled = amount, so a grant with one tranche Settled and the rest Failed/Voided has no exit; there is no Disbursing->Disbursing edge for the next tranche, no edge for a return of one tranche, and no headline or date rule for part-paid grants.

scenario: Split grant: tranche 1 settled 3 Mar (Final), tranche 2 settled 20 Mar (in return window); donor views status
permitted_outcome: Label states amount and date per tranche or 'Partly paid'; 'Paid' only when every tranche is Final
prohibited_outcome: Single 'Paid on 3 Mar' or 'Payment sent' with one date
finding_description: Rev 2 PA-1 permits split disbursement but the grant machine was not updated: Disbursing->Funded requires all attempts terminal WITHOUT settlement and Disbursing->Disbursed requires cumulative settled = amount, so a grant with one tranche Settled and the rest Failed/Voided has no exit; there is no Disbursing->Disbursing edge for the next tranche, no edge for a return of one tranche, and no headline or date rule for part-paid grants.

scenario: Donor asks to cancel while the wire attempt is Unknown
permitted_outcome: Cancellation request recorded as waiting for payment outcome; if Unknown resolves NotReceived the request is decided; if Accepted a recall is attempted
prohibited_outcome: StopRequested issued from Unknown with no machine edge; cancel silently dropped; grant Canceled while money may be in flight
finding_description: GR-3 (rev 2) says cancellation during Submitted or Unknown 'becomes a recall or stop request', but the attempt machine allows StopRequested only from Accepted. GR-9 has no 'waiting for payment outcome' state and does not say a pending request is re-evaluated (Granted) when the attempt later ends without settlement. Check attempts Unknown at the print vendor cannot use the positive-pay stop that is the natural resolution.

scenario: Check-printing vendor times out after file transmission; check attempt Unknown; vendor cannot prove non-printing
permitted_outcome: Positive-pay stop on the check number then reissue after bank-confirmed void
prohibited_outcome: Reissue on a new number while the first may be mailed; indefinite Unknown
finding_description: GR-3 (rev 2) says cancellation during Submitted or Unknown 'becomes a recall or stop request', but the attempt machine allows StopRequested only from Accepted. GR-9 has no 'waiting for payment outcome' state and does not say a pending request is re-evaluated (Granted) when the attempt later ends without settlement. Check attempts Unknown at the print vendor cannot use the positive-pay stop that is the natural resolution.

scenario: Cancellation request Requested while the attempt is Submitted; provider then rejects synchronously
permitted_outcome: Request is Granted automatically or routed to sponsor with the reject recorded; grant Canceled with reservation released
prohibited_outcome: Request left in Requested forever; new attempt created despite pending cancel
finding_description: GR-3 (rev 2) says cancellation during Submitted or Unknown 'becomes a recall or stop request', but the attempt machine allows StopRequested only from Accepted. GR-9 has no 'waiting for payment outcome' state and does not say a pending request is re-evaluated (Granted) when the attempt later ends without settlement. Check attempts Unknown at the print vendor cannot use the positive-pay stop that is the natural resolution.

scenario: Grant Returned then Canceled by sponsor (funds re-credited); the return is later dishonoured and the charity keeps the money
permitted_outcome: Double-payment/reversal child case; headline 'Canceled' plus note that the payment reached the recipient; fund debit reinstated under FI-38
prohibited_outcome: Headline 'Canceled' only, with fund holding cash that left
finding_description: Headline rule 1 (terminal decision outranks every payment label) and rule 4 (Paid to [Recipient]) ignore linked child cases created under SM-0/GR-6/PA-6/GR-12: a Canceled grant whose return was dishonoured, a Canceled grant whose voided check was paid, a Disbursed grant whose money went to an impostor account, and a grant blocked by a double-payment case all show a false or silent headline; the GR-12 replacement grant appears unlinked.

scenario: Payment Settled and Final to an impostor account (profile hijack); headline after Final
permitted_outcome: Donor label avoids 'Paid to [Charity]'; neutral 'Under review' class or sponsor-chosen disclosure; replacement grant linked to the original
prohibited_outcome: 'Paid to [Charity] on D' while the charity was never paid
finding_description: Headline rule 1 (terminal decision outranks every payment label) and rule 4 (Paid to [Recipient]) ignore linked child cases created under SM-0/GR-6/PA-6/GR-12: a Canceled grant whose return was dishonoured, a Canceled grant whose voided check was paid, a Disbursed grant whose money went to an impostor account, and a grant blocked by a double-payment case all show a false or silent headline; the GR-12 replacement grant appears unlinked.

scenario: Double-payment case open (PA-6) blocks further attempts on a Funded grant for 3 weeks
permitted_outcome: Donor sees a delay label; staff see the case
prohibited_outcome: Donor sees 'Ready to pay' or 'Payment being prepared' indefinitely
finding_description: Headline rule 1 (terminal decision outranks every payment label) and rule 4 (Paid to [Recipient]) ignore linked child cases created under SM-0/GR-6/PA-6/GR-12: a Canceled grant whose return was dishonoured, a Canceled grant whose voided check was paid, a Disbursed grant whose money went to an impostor account, and a grant blocked by a double-payment case all show a false or silent headline; the GR-12 replacement grant appears unlinked.

scenario: Monthly recurring instance to charity X is generated while last month's instance payment is Unknown
permitted_outcome: Instance proceeds or waits per defined rule; no duplicate-routing storm
prohibited_outcome: Each period's instance silently routed to a human queue; or the Unknown banner rule silently bypassed for system-generated instances
finding_description: Headline rule 2 routes 'a new recommendation to the same recipient from the same fund' to a human while a payment is Unknown. Scope is undefined for recurring instances (REC-6: each period would generate a referral, or silently bypass), for the same donor's other funds, and for co-advisors who never saw the Unknown banner.

scenario: While fund A's grant to charity X is Unknown, the donor recommends the same amount to X from their fund B; separately a co-advisor of A recommends to X
permitted_outcome: Routing to human covers same donor/recipient across funds and co-advisors, or rule explicitly scoped
prohibited_outcome: Duplicate silently approved because the key is fund-only
finding_description: Headline rule 2 routes 'a new recommendation to the same recipient from the same fund' to a human while a payment is Unknown. Scope is undefined for recurring instances (REC-6: each period would generate a referral, or silently bypass), for the same donor's other funds, and for co-advisors who never saw the Unknown banner.

scenario: Sanctions-match hold added after the wire was Submitted; donor (possibly the subject) views status
permitted_outcome: Donor sees 'Payment in progress' only; review disclosed per policy [C]
prohibited_outcome: 'Payment in progress - under review' tipping off a possible subject
finding_description: Headline rule 3 appends '- under review' to a donor-visible label when a hold is added after submission, while the vocabulary's PostPaymentReview row and GR-6 say post-payment review is staff-only unless policy discloses. For sanctions- or fraud-driven holds this is a disclosure the UX-F19 rule was meant to avoid [C: tipping-off].

scenario: Residual sweep fixed and Settled; 20 days later an earlier ACH grant from the fund is returned R03 while the fund is ClosurePending
permitted_outcome: Defined destination: re-pay original (GR-11), second sweep, or FI-35 residual destination
prohibited_outcome: Cash left in a fund that can never close or be swept
finding_description: FI-15 fixes a residual sweep 'after the last settlement', but earlier grants' return windows (and the sweep's own) are still open and contributions can still arrive while the fund is ClosurePending. Cash that arrives after the sweep is fixed but before Closed has no destination: GR-11 re-pay, a second sweep, or FI-35 (which applies only after closure).

scenario: Donor's employer-match check contribution arrives while the fund is ClosurePending after the residual sweep was fixed
permitted_outcome: Defined policy: reject/return, sweep again, or FI-35 destination; acknowledgment consistent
prohibited_outcome: Contribution accepted with units issued in a fund being swept
finding_description: FI-15 fixes a residual sweep 'after the last settlement', but earlier grants' return windows (and the sweep's own) are still open and contributions can still arrive while the fund is ClosurePending. Cash that arrives after the sweep is fixed but before Closed has no destination: GR-11 re-pay, a second sweep, or FI-35 (which applies only after closure).

scenario: Return of a $10,000 grant arrives net of $50 fees in an over-committed fund; charge bearer = fund
permitted_outcome: $9,950 re-reserved under GR-11; $50 top-up decided by explicit rule (allowed exception or sponsor-funded)
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay blocked by FI-12 with no label; or $9,950 paid in breach of GR-1
finding_description: GR-11 exempts only 'returned money re-reserved' from FI-12. When the return is net of fees or a foreign-currency grant's return converts at a different rate, the top-up needed to re-pay the GR-1 fixed amount is a new reservation that FI-12 refuses in an over-committed fund; there is no state or label for a grant that cannot be re-paid in full.

scenario: EUR-fixed foreign grant returned; returned EUR converts to fewer USD than were consumed; fund over-committed
permitted_outcome: FX difference borne per FI-31 under an explicit GR-11 extension
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay refused under FI-12; or re-paid in USD
finding_description: GR-11 exempts only 'returned money re-reserved' from FI-12. When the return is net of fees or a foreign-currency grant's return converts at a different rate, the top-up needed to re-pay the GR-1 fixed amount is a new reservation that FI-12 refuses in an over-committed fund; there is no state or label for a grant that cannot be re-paid in full.

scenario: Check voided (bank-confirmed) in a fund that has since become over-committed; sponsor wants to reissue
permitted_outcome: Outstanding-check liability reverses into a restored commitment (like GR-11) and reissue proceeds
prohibited_outcome: Reservation stuck Consumed; reissue refused by FI-12; capacity double-counted
finding_description: PA-4 (rev 2) consumes the reservation at check issue. After a bank-confirmed void the reservation is Consumed, yet the reservation states and FI-07 have no path from Consumed back to Active, and GR-11's exemption covers returns, not voids. Reissue in an over-committed or held fund is therefore either impossible or an unstated exception.

scenario: Check voided for a grant whose donor fund was Suspended between issue and void
permitted_outcome: Liability reversed to fund cash; reissue held by GR-7; label 'Check voided - on hold'
prohibited_outcome: Automatic reissue; reservation left Consumed with no grant claim
finding_description: PA-4 (rev 2) consumes the reservation at check issue. After a bank-confirmed void the reservation is Consumed, yet the reservation states and FI-07 have no path from Consumed back to Active, and GR-11's exemption covers returns, not voids. Reissue in an over-committed or held fund is therefore either impossible or an unstated exception.

scenario: Attempt declared Lost (provider receivership) and replacement paid; 8 months later the receiver distributes the original payment to the charity
permitted_outcome: Double-payment case and recovery opened as for other contradicted terminal states
prohibited_outcome: No case opened because Lost is not in the PA-6 list
finding_description: PA-6 lists Failed, NotReceived, Returned, Voided and ResolvedByDecision as terminal states whose contradiction opens a double-payment case. It omits Lost (added in rev 2) and Rejected, so a Lost payment later delivered by a receiver, or a synchronously rejected item that the provider processed anyway, does not block the replacement attempt.

scenario: Provider returns synchronous Rejected; a new attempt is created; the original item appears settled in the next day's report
permitted_outcome: Double-payment case; further attempts blocked
prohibited_outcome: Second payment proceeds; Rejected treated as proof of non-processing
finding_description: PA-6 lists Failed, NotReceived, Returned, Voided and ResolvedByDecision as terminal states whose contradiction opens a double-payment case. It omits Lost (added in rev 2) and Rejected, so a Lost payment later delivered by a receiver, or a synchronously rejected item that the provider processed anyway, does not block the replacement attempt.

scenario: Pre-funded provider (one aggregate daily debit) leaves one item of 300 Unknown; provider gives non-receipt proof
permitted_outcome: Bank-side evidence defined per adapter (e.g., provider-ledger statement and batch total net of items) enabling NotReceived
prohibited_outcome: Every such item forced into two-person ResolvedByDecision; or provider proof alone accepted
finding_description: PA-2's second source ('bank statement shows no debit') is not observable per item for pre-funded, batch-funded or net-settled providers (one aggregate debit, PA-8) or for checks (debit only at presentment). For these rails every Unknown falls through to two-person ResolvedByDecision; the per-adapter evidence table in PA-6 must define the bank-side proof per rail.

scenario: Unauthenticated email reports donor's death on Dec 20; donor's December standing ACH contribution is due Dec 27
permitted_outcome: Debit continues pending verification (AUTH-I5) or policy states the tax-timing risk and notifies the verified channel
prohibited_outcome: Debit suspended on a false notice; deduction moves to next year without the donor knowing
finding_description: AUTH-I5 limits an unauthenticated death notice to holding new recommendations and template instances, but state models section 5 (TVF-120) suspends standing contribution debits on a death notice without distinguishing verified from unverified. A false notice in late December can stop a donor's contribution and move their deduction to the next tax year.

scenario: Fraud recall must be sent while payment-gate clock skew exceeds tolerance
permitted_outcome: Stop/recall and observation recording still permitted; only new submissions fail closed
prohibited_outcome: Recall blocked by fail-closed rule; settlement observation rejected
finding_description: TIME-2 fails closed 'for money movement' on clock skew, without exempting protective actions: stop, recall and void requests, and recording of settlement or return observations (SM-4 says holds never block these). A skewed payment-gate node could block a fraud recall.

scenario: $400k human-approved grant in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity; capacity frees by $400k over 10 days but routine $5k grants keep reserving it
permitted_outcome: Defined priority for waiting approved grants, or stated starvation policy
prohibited_outcome: Large grant starved until expiry with 'Approved - waiting for funds' shown throughout
finding_description: ApprovedAwaitingCapacity grants hold no reservation, so under GR-10 they have no ordering key: new routine grants, which approve and reserve atomically, take freed capacity first and can starve a large human-approved grant until it expires. The FI-06 displayed 'available' does not subtract them, and nothing says whether the expiry clock runs while the fund is Frozen, Suspended or held.

scenario: Grant in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity; donor's dashboard shows available amount
permitted_outcome: Available estimate subtracts waiting approved grants
prohibited_outcome: Available shows the full capacity, inviting new recommendations that take precedence
finding_description: ApprovedAwaitingCapacity grants hold no reservation, so under GR-10 they have no ordering key: new routine grants, which approve and reserve atomically, take freed capacity first and can starve a large human-approved grant until it expires. The FI-06 displayed 'available' does not subtract them, and nothing says whether the expiry clock runs while the fund is Frozen, Suspended or held.

scenario: Fund Frozen by court order for 4 months while a grant waits in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity with a 60-day expiry
permitted_outcome: Expiry clock rule stated (pauses or runs) with notice
prohibited_outcome: Grant auto-Canceled during a freeze by timer alone
finding_description: ApprovedAwaitingCapacity grants hold no reservation, so under GR-10 they have no ordering key: new routine grants, which approve and reserve atomically, take freed capacity first and can starve a large human-approved grant until it expires. The FI-06 displayed 'available' does not subtract them, and nothing says whether the expiry clock runs while the fund is Frozen, Suspended or held.

scenario: Closure requested; zero reservations, all attempts terminal and Final; one sponsor-approved grant waits in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity
permitted_outcome: Closure blocked or the grant explicitly ended with notice
prohibited_outcome: Fund Closed (FUND-1 met) with a live approved grant
finding_description: FUND-1 (closure), FUND-3 (lineage routing) and FI-15 (residual sweep) test reservations and attempts only. Grants in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity, UnderReview or AwaitingHumanDecision, open GR-9 cancellation requests and open post-payment or double-payment cases are not preconditions, so a fund can close or merge with a sponsor-approved grant waiting.

scenario: Fund A merged into B while an A grant is in AwaitingHumanDecision and another has an open GR-9 cancellation request
permitted_outcome: Lineage table routes both to B or ends them explicitly
prohibited_outcome: Items orphaned on a closed source fund
finding_description: FUND-1 (closure), FUND-3 (lineage routing) and FI-15 (residual sweep) test reservations and attempts only. Grants in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity, UnderReview or AwaitingHumanDecision, open GR-9 cancellation requests and open post-payment or double-payment cases are not preconditions, so a fund can close or merge with a sponsor-approved grant waiting.

scenario: Proceeds-linked grant approved; stock sold in 3 lots over 3 weeks; sponsor fee accrues between
permitted_outcome: Defined fixing at final lot; gross/net rule; label 'Approved - amount set when sale completes'
prohibited_outcome: Grant fixed at first lot; or reserved at an estimate; or no label
finding_description: Proceeds-linked (FI-39) and residual-sweep (FI-15) grants are approved before their amount is fixed, but the grant machine needs an amount to reach Reserved and the headline has no label for 'approved, amount set when the sale completes'. Also undefined: multi-lot sales, whether proceeds are gross or net of sponsor fees and FI-36 charges, and capacity treatment before fixing.

scenario: Residual-sweep grant approved; fund ClosurePending; donor views status for 70 days awaiting last Final
permitted_outcome: Label explains amount not yet known
prohibited_outcome: Headline shows 'Approved by Sponsor' with an amount
finding_description: Proceeds-linked (FI-39) and residual-sweep (FI-15) grants are approved before their amount is fixed, but the grant machine needs an amount to reach Reserved and the headline has no label for 'approved, amount set when the sale completes'. Also undefined: multi-lot sales, whether proceeds are gross or net of sponsor fees and FI-36 charges, and capacity treatment before fixing.

scenario: LP capital call of $200k (FI-37 commitment) arrives after grants reserved all capacity; fund over-committed
permitted_outcome: Pre-decided priority between binding commitments/taxes and reserved grants
prohibited_outcome: Ad-hoc incident decision; grant canceled silently; call defaulted
finding_description: FI-26/OD-10 set the priority between fees and approved grants in over-commitment, but not for FI-37 charges and commitments (capital calls, carrying costs, UBIT/990-T tax). A legally owed tax or a binding capital call that arrives after grants were reserved has no stated priority.

scenario: 990-T UBIT tax allocated to a fund whose capacity is fully reserved for approved grants
permitted_outcome: Tax paid per stated priority; grants follow over-commitment policy
prohibited_outcome: Tax unpaid or fund negative
finding_description: FI-26/OD-10 set the priority between fees and approved grants in over-commitment, but not for FI-37 charges and commitments (capital calls, carrying costs, UBIT/990-T tax). A legally owed tax or a binding capital call that arrives after grants were reserved has no stated priority.

scenario: Donor's agent edits five Submitted recommendations (supersession); replacements wait for donor confirmation that never comes
permitted_outcome: Originals stay live until replacement is Submitted
prohibited_outcome: Originals Withdrawn immediately; replacements Expire; donor's grants vanish
finding_description: REC-5 withdraws the linked grant in the same operation as supersession. When an agent or delegate edits a submitted recommendation and the replacement waits in AwaitingRequesterConfirmation, the original grant is already Withdrawn. A compromised or faulty agent can cancel a donor's pending recommendations without confirmation, and an expired confirmation leaves nothing.

scenario: Unverified death notice; donor's $30k recommendation already Submitted and in UnderReview
permitted_outcome: Item routed to human review (consistent with REC-3); verified channel notified
prohibited_outcome: Approved by policy and completed under GR-8 although authority may have lapsed
finding_description: AUTH-I5's limited effect covers only new recommendations. A recommendation already Submitted but undecided from the named person is approved normally and then protected by GR-8. REC-3 requires that a recommendation not be decided under lapsed authority, so an unverified notice should route such items to human review.

scenario: Private-benefit flag after submission opened a post-payment review; the wire is then returned (account closed)
permitted_outcome: Re-pay held while review is open; donor label neutral
prohibited_outcome: Automatic re-pay to the recipient under review; label 'arranging payment again'
finding_description: GR-6 post-payment review is a child case, not a hold. After a return (Disbursed->Funded, 're-pay permitted'), SM-6 re-checks holds and eligibility but not open review cases, so the re-payment can go to a recipient under a private-benefit or fraud review, while the donor is told payment is being arranged again.

scenario: Duplicate settlement observed for a grant whose reservation is already Consumed (contradicted NotReceived)
permitted_outcome: Settlement recorded against error-cost suspense/receivable per OD-20; fund not charged; case opened
prohibited_outcome: Settlement rejected by FI-17 and left unrecorded; or posted to the donor fund
finding_description: FI-17 settlement conservation reduces 'the matching reservation by X' in one transaction or fails. A settlement in excess of the reservation (PA-6 duplicate, a ResolvedByDecision or Lost exception, a recovered Lost payment) cannot be posted, although SM-4 says external observations are always recorded. Excess outflow needs a defined posting to an error-cost suspense or receivable account (OD-20), never to the donor fund.

scenario: Provider defunct; attempt Unknown; charity's audited bank statement confirms receipt
permitted_outcome: ResolvedByDecision with outcome 'deemed settled'; grant Disbursed; Final computed from decision
prohibited_outcome: Grant returns to Funded and invites re-payment; Final never computable
finding_description: ResolvedByDecision has no recorded outcome. A human who concludes the payment did reach the charity (provider defunct, charity confirms receipt) has no 'deemed settled' resolution, so the grant derivation treats every decision as non-settlement: the grant returns to Funded, re-payment is invited, and Final and Reconciled cannot be computed.

scenario: Grant Returned while the fund is Suspended (GR-7 hold on re-pay)
permitted_outcome: Headline 'On hold' or 'Returned - on hold'
prohibited_outcome: 'Returned - we are arranging payment again' while re-pay is blocked
finding_description: Headline rule 5 ('Returned - we are arranging payment again') outranks rule 6 (hold), and it applies before the sponsor has chosen between re-pay and cancel (Disbursed->Funded vs Disbursed->Canceled). A Suspended or Frozen fund (GR-7) or an undecided sponsor therefore shows a promise that may not be kept.

scenario: Grant Returned; sponsor has not yet decided between re-pay and cancel
permitted_outcome: Neutral label 'Payment returned - we will update you'
prohibited_outcome: Promise of re-payment before the decision
finding_description: Headline rule 5 ('Returned - we are arranging payment again') outranks rule 6 (hold), and it applies before the sponsor has chosen between re-pay and cancel (Disbursed->Funded vs Disbursed->Canceled). A Suspended or Frozen fund (GR-7) or an undecided sponsor therefore shows a promise that may not be kept.

scenario: Donor requests closure; last grant was by check, issued 4 months ago and not presented
permitted_outcome: Outstanding-check liability transferred to sponsor-level unclaimed-property liability so the fund can close
prohibited_outcome: Closure blocked for years; or check voided solely to close
finding_description: FUND-1 requires every attempt to be terminal, but an issued check stays Accepted until presented, voided or escheated, which can take years under dormancy rules. Escheated is called a check disposition (section 2) but is still absent from the section 3 diagram (the rev-2 fix for TVS-222 is incomplete). No rule transfers an outstanding-check liability to the sponsor level so the fund can close.

scenario: Routine recurring instance fails capacity at atomic approve+reserve
permitted_outcome: Defined outcome (held for retry with order, declined with notice, or referred)
prohibited_outcome: Implementer chooses; FI-09 'held' contradicts GR-10 atomicity
finding_description: GR-10 makes routine approval and reservation atomic and reserves ApprovedAwaitingCapacity for human-approved large grants. The outcome for a routine grant or a recurring instance that fails capacity is undefined (decline, refer, or retry). FI-05's on-violation text ('stays Approved and held') and FI-09 ('instance held') still describe the rev-1 model (a TVC-036 remnant).

scenario: Cancellation request on an Accepted ACH; stop fails and settlement arrives
permitted_outcome: GR-9 Overtaken with label 'could not be stopped - paid on D'
prohibited_outcome: Grant shown Canceled

scenario: Sponsor cancels a Reserved grant whose Prepared attempt exists
permitted_outcome: Attempt Abandoned in the same operation; reservation released
prohibited_outcome: Orphan Prepared attempt released later

scenario: Donor enrols a new passkey (cooling-off) and a pre-cleared giving-plan item to a recipient added 3 days earlier executes
permitted_outcome: Fresh step-up plus sponsor-direct confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Plan item executes on the earlier clearance

scenario: Agent-created recurring template amended by the agent to raise the amount
permitted_outcome: Principal confirmation required for the amendment
prohibited_outcome: Amendment applied silently

scenario: False death notice cleared by the donor via the verified channel after two monthly instances were held
permitted_outcome: Held instances follow the template's stated missed-run policy
prohibited_outcome: Both silently skipped or both double-fired

scenario: Unknown aging deadline lands on a bank holiday weekend
permitted_outcome: Deadline computed in the rail's business-day calendar; exception owner named
prohibited_outcome: Wall-clock expiry triggers premature escalation or retry

scenario: Retry of an Unknown attempt one hour after the provider's 24h deduplication window closed
permitted_outcome: Treated as a new attempt requiring PA-2 first
prohibited_outcome: Same key reused outside the window

scenario: Pool cash reconciliation break of $40k on a shared custodial account during December
permitted_outcome: Reservations reduced only by the unexplained break amount
prohibited_outcome: All donors' reservations blocked

scenario: Grant paid from fund A by sponsor sourcing error instead of donor's fund B; B lacks capacity
permitted_outcome: Inter-fund reclassification; sponsor makes A whole under OD-20
prohibited_outcome: B goes negative; A silently bears it

scenario: Partner changes the SCIM external ID for a donor after a directory migration
permitted_outcome: Dual control and donor notice before remapping
prohibited_outcome: Automatic remap by email match

scenario: Human-approved percentage grant waits 3 weeks in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity while NAV falls 12%
permitted_outcome: Amount stays as fixed at approval (FI-10); reserves when capacity allows
prohibited_outcome: Re-fixed at reservation

scenario: Dormant check reaches state escheat date; no Escheated edge exists
permitted_outcome: Escheat disposition with liability transfer
prohibited_outcome: Void-and-recredit contrary to unclaimed-property law

scenario: Pre-funded provider debits sponsor, then reports Failed; grant goes back to Funded and shows 'Ready to pay' though cash is a provider receivable
permitted_outcome: Grant held until receivable collected
prohibited_outcome: New attempt funded from cash still at provider

scenario: Wire returned voluntarily by the beneficiary bank 5 months after 'Paid to [Recipient]' (Final) was shown
permitted_outcome: Linked return; headline changes with explanation
prohibited_outcome: Return refused because Final

scenario: SIM-swapped attacker changes phone; sponsor-direct confirmation for a new recipient goes to the hijacked phone
permitted_outcome: Confirmation through pre-change channel
prohibited_outcome: Confirmation to the new phone

scenario: Attacker with ATO submits routine grants to an attacker-controlled charity; once approved, files an unauthenticated death notice for the real donor. AUTH-I5 holds 'new recommendations and requests' from the donor, which the donor's cancellation request and fraud report are routed as; GR-8 completes the approved grants
permitted_outcome: Principal-level hold never blocks cancellation requests, fraud reports, credential recovery or authority-protective actions; a fraud report on approved-unpaid grants places a grant hold (SM-4/SM-5)
prohibited_outcome: Victim is silenced while GR-8 pays the attacker's grants
finding_description: AUTH-I5 defines the hold by requester (all new requests from the named person) but does not exempt protective requests. SM-4's exemption for cancellation applies to object holds, not principal holds. Requirement: a principal hold under AUTH-I5 exempts cancellation/stop requests, fraud reports and recovery; any fraud report from the named person or verified channel places a grant hold on approved-unpaid grants before GR-8 completion applies.

scenario: Mass unauthenticated death notices filed on Dec 27 for 300 donors; the TVF-120 rule suspends their standing December contribution debits; donors lose the contribution in the intended tax year
permitted_outcome: Unauthenticated notice is a flag only; contribution suspension requires a verified notice or the donor's own instruction via verified channel
prohibited_outcome: A false notice suspends contributions and causes tax-year harm, contradicting AUTH-I5's 'delays at most own requests'
finding_description: State-models §5 suspends standing contribution debits 'on a death notice' without distinguishing authenticated from unauthenticated notices, so AUTH-I5's bounded-harm claim is false. Requirement: debit suspension only on verified notice (or donor instruction); unauthenticated notices trigger verified-channel contact; rate-limit and pattern-detect bulk notices.

scenario: Patient attacker takes over an account in April, waits out the AUTH-I7 cooling-off, adds an attacker charity to the giving plan in June, and waits beyond the REC-7 look-back window; the December pre-cleared item executes without step-up
permitted_outcome: Re-confirmation is required for any recipient added since the principal's last confirmation through a channel that predates the account's last credential/recovery change
prohibited_outcome: Execution without fresh confirmation because the wall-clock look-back elapsed
finding_description: REC-7 and AUTH-I7 are wall-clock windows; an attacker defeats both by waiting. TVF-153's grooming chain survives whenever the plan horizon exceeds the look-back. Requirement: recipient novelty and re-confirmation are measured relative to the last confirmation through a pre-existing verified channel, not elapsed time; look-back must be at least the plan pre-clearance horizon.

scenario: Fifty accounts are taken over separately (credential stuffing); each adds the same newly listed charity with one small recommendation per fund. REC-7's cross-fund flag sees one fund per principal and never fires
permitted_outcome: A recipient-side fan-in signal (many unrelated principals newly adding the same recently registered recipient) raises a flag and holds release
prohibited_outcome: Per-principal velocity is the only defense against a distributed campaign
finding_description: All velocity and cross-fund controls are keyed on the requester. No control aggregates by recipient. Requirement: recipient fan-in monitor (new-recipient additions by unrelated principals, weighted by recipient age and bank-change recency) that raises add-only flags (SM-5) and holds release above threshold.

scenario: Wealth-firm partner is acquired and moves 40,000 users to the acquirer's IdP: every issuer+subject changes. AUTH-I8 requires dual control and donor notice per mapping change; ops request a bulk remap file
permitted_outcome: Class-level remap is a governed domain command: partner-signed old-to-new mapping, per-row match on a stable attribute, donor notice, sampling, and rows that fail stay unmapped (donor re-binds via sponsor channel)
prohibited_outcome: A bulk file approved once under dual control; a malicious or wrong row maps an attacker to a donor
finding_description: AUTH-I8 is per-subject; partner IdP migration or M&A is a class event with no procedure, so staff will improvise a bulk remap (cf. TVF-149 for flags). Requirement: a bulk identity-remap procedure with signed partner manifest, row-level verification, sampling and donor notice; unverified rows fail closed.

scenario: Sponsor A detects that a charity's bank-change request on the shared payee registry was fraudulent. The tenant term blocks A's finding from becoming sponsor B's decision input; B's weaker process accepted the same change and pays the attacker
permitted_outcome: Positive trust (verification) never crosses tenants; negative signals (fraud alerts, suspected compromise) may raise add-only flags and holds in other tenants, with B's own review deciding
prohibited_outcome: Tenant isolation suppresses fraud intelligence across sponsors
finding_description: The rev-2 tenant term ('one tenant's verification or change never becomes another tenant's decision input') is symmetric and therefore also blocks warnings. Requirement: distinguish trust-conferring inputs (never shared) from risk-raising inputs (may flag/hold, never clear) across tenants, subject to data-sharing terms.

scenario: Point-in-time restore on Dec 29 brings payee and policy stores back to T-12 min while the command-event store restores to T-4 min. OD-22's match check finds payee rows with no matching event (and events with no rows); every payment fails closed and ops ask to disable the check
permitted_outcome: Restore runbook re-establishes a common consistency point and replays commands; unmatched rows stay blocked per payee, not globally; the match check is never disabled; break-glass during command-service outage is itself a pre-defined domain procedure
prohibited_outcome: Year-end payment halt or the match check disabled under pressure
finding_description: OD-22's 'every authoritative change matched to a command event before payment' has no defined behavior after restore or when the command service itself is down. Requirement: DR restores data and command stores to a common point (or replays); match failures block per object; a pre-approved degraded break-glass path exists that still emits command events.

scenario: Cutover imports 9,000 charity bank profiles and 2,000 giving-plan recipients from the incumbent as one bulk load approved by dual control; one row was altered in the incumbent export
permitted_outcome: Each imported record enters through a per-record import command with source provenance; imported bank details are unverified until re-verified or matched to an incumbent-paid history; REC-7 treats incumbent plan recipients by incumbent add date only with evidence
prohibited_outcome: A bulk load satisfies OD-22 as one command; tampered rows become verified payees
finding_description: Migration is the largest write to payee and plan data, but OD-22 and REC-7 do not say how imported records get provenance, verification status or an 'added' time. Requirement: per-record import commands; imported payees start Unverified unless matched to settled incumbent payments; REC-7 add-time from incumbent evidence or import time.

scenario: Insider with write access edits the routine-threshold policy row directly, lets 600 grants auto-approve over 3 hours, and reverts the row. At payment, OD-22's match check compares current data to command events and finds them consistent
permitted_outcome: Payment re-check verifies the decision's input-snapshot hash (SM-1) against state derivable from command events at decision time; mismatch holds the grant
prohibited_outcome: Edit-and-revert passes a check that inspects only current state
finding_description: OD-22 matching is stated 'before payment' on authoritative data, not on the inputs used at decision. Requirement: every decision's input snapshot (policy version, authority revision, payee revision) must be reproducible from the command-event log; SM-6 verifies it at release.

scenario: An intermediary bank blocks a wire to a foreign charity under its own OFAC program; the provider reports neither settlement nor failure. PA-5 ages the attempt; ops propose ResolvedByDecision and re-pay to a substitute charity
permitted_outcome: A third-party Blocked outcome: funds are a blocked receivable, not Lost or NotReceived; no re-pay of that amount; sanctions officer and GC review; reporting obligations of each party recorded
prohibited_outcome: Re-payment treated as safe or the amount written off as a provider loss
finding_description: TVCTL-13 adds a sponsor-side Blocked disposition, but blocking by an intermediary or provider has no outcome. PA-2/Lost would misclassify it. Requirement: attempt outcome BlockedByThirdParty with a blocked-receivable accounting treatment, no re-pay of the blocked amount, and reporting coordination.

scenario: Giving plans pre-clear 30,000 December items; 40% of recipients were added in Q4 (normal giving season) so REC-7 demands fresh step-up for each in the last week of December; 6,000 confirmations expire unseen
permitted_outcome: Confirmation collected when the plan item is cleared through a verified channel; re-confirmation only where assurance at add-time was below threshold; expiries notified with a sponsor-direct action
prohibited_outcome: REC-7 recreates the December surge that alternative 2D was meant to remove; plan items lapse silently
finding_description: Rev-2 REC-7 creates a new operational failure path: it shifts confirmation load back into peak and lets items expire. Requirement: model REC-7 load in economics; front-load confirmation at plan clearance; risk-based re-confirmation; expiry produces a visible donor status.

scenario: Payment provider de-risks the sponsor on Dec 1 (TVS-098). Verified bank details are stored only as provider tokens, so the sponsor must re-collect bank details from 9,000 charities in December; fraudsters send lookalike 're-enrolment' emails
permitted_outcome: Sponsor holds verified bank details (or a portable escrowed token) independently of any provider; a provider switch is not a bank-detail change and triggers no charity re-collection
prohibited_outcome: Mass re-enrolment at year-end becomes cover for bank-change fraud
finding_description: The baseline expects 'profile re-enrollment' on provider exit (TVS-098), which at scale is the ideal phishing pretext. Requirement: provider-independent custody of verified payee bank data (or contractual token export), with provider migration tested in drills.

scenario: Sponsor's disbursement bank enters receivership on a Friday in December; $40M of Funded-grant cash above insured limits is in the account; 1,200 attempts are Submitted/Unknown
permitted_outcome: Funded cash is a claim on the bank; grants move to a funding-impaired condition; attempts resolved by two-source evidence from the receiver; loss-bearer per OD-20
prohibited_outcome: Funded treated as cash on hand; attempts retried from a new bank, creating duplicates
governing_rules: GR state Funded; PA-1; PA-8; OD-20
finding_description: No workflow covers failure or de-risking of the sponsor's own operating/disbursement bank (TVF-122 covers custodian and processor only). Requirement: bank-failure workflow, uninsured-balance concentration limit and multi-bank disbursement design.

scenario: Sponsor's operating bank closes the disbursement account with 30 days' notice in December; 800 issued checks are outstanding (PA-4 Accepted); presentments after closure are returned to charities
permitted_outcome: Outstanding checks are voided via the bank before closure or honoured via a successor account; charities notified; void/reissue follows PA-4
prohibited_outcome: Checks bounce; attempts stuck Accepted with no Voided confirmation possible
finding_description: Same gap as K-13: bank de-risking of the sponsor has no procedure for outstanding checks and positive pay. Requirement: account-exit runbook with check-population settlement before closure.

scenario: Model provider tightens its safety filter; AG-02 returns a refusal or truncated output for grant purposes mentioning certain topics. The integration parses 'no benefit indicators found' from the empty result
permitted_outcome: A refusal, filter, truncation or schema failure is 'no result' and triggers the deterministic fallback (TVCTL-05); refusal rate monitored
prohibited_outcome: Refusal read as a negative finding; benefit-tainted grants auto-approve
finding_description: TVCTL-05 requires an agent result or fallback but does not define what counts as a result. Requirement: typed agent outcomes (Result / NoResult / Refused / Invalid); only a schema-valid Result counts; refusal and filter rates are KRIs.

scenario: Model provider announces deprecation of the pinned snapshot effective Dec 15; revalidation of the replacement needs model-risk sign-off that cannot finish before peak
permitted_outcome: Contract guarantees snapshot availability for a stated horizon and no forced change in a sponsor-declared freeze; otherwise the agent is retired to its fallback, not swapped unvalidated
prohibited_outcome: Unvalidated replacement deployed under the same name, or all affected screens fall to backlog without plan
finding_description: TVF-140 pins snapshots but does not cover provider-forced deprecation timing. Requirement: model contracts include availability horizon and change-freeze windows; a pre-validated alternate or explicit fallback plan per agent.

scenario: Restore to T-15 min loses an advisor revocation and a donor's new-passkey enrolment record; after restore the advisor's authority is active again and the AUTH-I7 cooling-off clock is absent, so grants to new recipients skip sponsor-direct confirmation
permitted_outcome: Security-relevant state (revocations, credential changes, holds, model flags, cooling-off start times) is re-derived after restore from authoritative sources (IdP logs, flag log) and the system fails closed until reconciled
prohibited_outcome: Restore resurrects revoked authority and erases cooling-off
finding_description: DR analysis (TVF-144) covers payment-gate vs decisioning RPO, not loss of security state. Requirement: security-state events have RPO 0 or are re-derivable from external authoritative logs; post-restore reconciliation of revocations, holds and credential timestamps before money movement.

scenario: A model-raised hold placed 6 minutes before an outage is lost in the RPO window; the grant is released after restore
permitted_outcome: Holds are add-only events replicated at T0 RPO; restore cannot remove a hold without a release event
prohibited_outcome: Lost hold silently released by restore
finding_description: Same root as K-16: hold/flag state needs RPO at least as strict as the payment gate.

scenario: Incumbent identified donors by email. Cutover lets donors 'claim' migrated accounts by email link; an attacker controlling a donor's stale email (or a recycled domain) claims a $2M fund
permitted_outcome: Account claim requires identity proofing against incumbent-verified attributes or a sponsor-mailed code; claims start an AUTH-I7 cooling-off; first new-recipient grants need sponsor-direct confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Possession of an email becomes fund control at cutover
finding_description: AUTH-I8 forbids email as a permanent identifier, but migration has no other binding available. Requirement: migrated-account claim protocol with proofing, cooling-off and notice to incumbent-verified address and phone.

scenario: A provider bug replays stale settlement webhooks for 3,000 previously Failed attempts in late December; PA-6 opens double-payment cases and blocks re-pay on all 3,000 grants
permitted_outcome: Contradicting evidence must come from an authenticated source and be checked against the bank; unauthenticated or unsupported claims open an inquiry without blocking; a bulk PA-6 triage procedure exists
prohibited_outcome: Rev-2 PA-6 becomes a denial-of-service lever on re-payment at peak
finding_description: PA-6 blocks on any 'evidence of settlement' without stating evidence quality, and has no bulk path. Requirement: evidence-source grading in adapter contracts; blocking only on authenticated or bank-corroborated evidence; class-level triage.

scenario: Provider pre-funds from a pooled account and settles net daily. For an Unknown attempt, provider says not received and the sponsor's bank shows no individual debit (it never shows per-item debits). PA-2 moves it to NotReceived; a new attempt is sent; both settle
permitted_outcome: For net or pre-funded settlement, 'no bank debit' is not evidence; second source must be an independent provider ledger statement or beneficiary-side confirmation, else ResolvedByDecision
prohibited_outcome: Two-source rule satisfied by a source that cannot observe the item
finding_description: PA-2's second source assumes per-item debits. Requirement: each provider adapter declares which evidence sources can observe an item; PA-2 accepts only sources that can.

scenario: Provider holding $60M in transit during the last week of December enters receivership; OD-20 recommends the sponsor make funds whole; the sponsor's unrestricted reserves are $15M
permitted_outcome: Per-provider in-transit exposure limit sized to sponsor reserves and insurance; exposure monitored daily; excess routed to another rail
prohibited_outcome: Sponsor-borne loss exceeds reserves, threatening sponsor solvency (FUND-4)
finding_description: OD-20's loss-bearer rule has no capacity check. Requirement: in-transit concentration limit per provider and per day, tied to reserves and insurance cover; peak batching plans respect it.

scenario: Insider uploads a fabricated board resolution extending routine-path delegation; TVCTL-09 links policy version P-14 to it and the routine path continues after the real delegation lapsed
