permitted_outcome: Delegation records enter only through a domain command attested by the corporate secretary via an independent channel, with the resolution hash recorded in board minutes
prohibited_outcome: Policy-delegation linkage checks existence, not authenticity
finding_description: TVCTL-09 links decisions to a delegation but nothing authenticates the delegation record itself. Requirement: delegation records are standing data under OD-22 with secretary attestation and annual Audit Committee reconciliation to minutes.

scenario: Provider's admin console is compromised; the beneficiary account behind a charity's provider token is changed at the provider. Sponsor payee profile unchanged; CTL-004 cooling-off never fires; provider reports Settled; bank debit matches
permitted_outcome: Provider confirmations echo a destination-account fingerprint compared to the sponsor's verified profile; beneficiary-bank name/account verification where available; mismatch opens a case before further payments
prohibited_outcome: Payments silently redirected for weeks until charities complain
finding_description: All payee-integrity controls inspect sponsor-side data. Destination substitution at the provider is invisible to ledger-bank-provider three-way match. Requirement: end-to-end destination attestation per settled attempt and periodic charity-side confirmation of receipt for new or changed destinations.

scenario: Staffer with custodian portal access initiates a free delivery of securities from a pool to an outside account; no platform command exists; three-way match (ledger, bank, provider) does not include custody positions until the monthly position reconciliation
permitted_outcome: Every external register movement (custodian, bank portal, IdP admin) requires a matching platform command event with dual control; custody positions are reconciled daily and unmatched movements hold the pool
prohibited_outcome: OD-22 protects platform stores while the same assets move through external registers
finding_description: OD-22 and TVR-PAY-004 cover platform data and payments, not custodial asset movements or other external authority registers. Requirement: extend OD-22 to external registers: custodian dual authorization bound to platform command IDs, daily custody-movement matching, alerting on unmatched movements.

scenario: IdP vendor's support staff, socially engineered, enrol a new passkey on a donor account through the IdP admin API; the sponsor platform never receives a credential-change event, so AUTH-I7 cooling-off does not start
permitted_outcome: IdP admin and API credential changes stream to the sponsor and must match sponsor-approved commands; unmatched changes revoke the credential and start AUTH-I7
prohibited_outcome: AUTH-I7 depends on change events the sponsor does not observe
finding_description: Same root as K-23 applied to identity: credential registers held by vendors are outside OD-22 matching.

scenario: Attacker compromises the donor's consumer cloud account and obtains the synced passkey. No enrolment event occurs, so AUTH-I7 never triggers; phishing-resistant step-up is satisfied; attacker adds a new recipient and recommends $45k
permitted_outcome: High-value or new-recipient actions need a factor outside the synced-credential ecosystem or sponsor-direct confirmation; anomaly on new device/location even with a valid passkey
prohibited_outcome: Synced passkey treated as proof of the principal; AUTH-I7 bypassed without any credential change
governing_rules: AUTH-I7; TVCTL-06; identity federation AAL table
finding_description: AUTH-I7 assumes takeover requires a credential change. Synced passkeys move with the cloud account. Requirement: assurance policy distinguishes synced from device-bound credentials for new-recipient and high-value actions; device-binding or sponsor-direct confirmation required.

scenario: AG-16 improvement agent drafts a threshold change; one policy officer 'reviews and publishes' it. SoD-2 (author ≠ publisher) is treated as satisfied because the agent is the author
permitted_outcome: An agent-drafted change is authored by the human who commissioned or accepted it; publishing needs a second human; the agent's draft is evidence, not an author
prohibited_outcome: SoD-2 collapses to a single human
governing_rules: SoD-2; DD-011; rule 1 (authority changes are human)
finding_description: SoD rules name roles but not how agent authorship counts. Requirement: agents can never satisfy one side of a pairwise SoD constraint; the commissioning human is the author of record.

scenario: Donor loses phone on Dec 26 and re-enrols a passkey; AUTH-I7 cooling-off means grants to new recipients need sponsor-direct confirmation, but every prior channel is gone
permitted_outcome: Assisted-channel proofing per TVR-SEC-007 with attribution; grants to existing recipients proceed
prohibited_outcome: Either support bypasses step-up by phone or the donor is excluded with no path

scenario: Partner reissues a departed advisor's SCIM externalId to a new hire
permitted_outcome: AUTH-I8 forbids reusable identifiers; partner contract attests externalId permanence; issuer+subject also checked; mismatch fails closed
prohibited_outcome: Mapping follows the recycled ID

scenario: Donor becomes SDN-listed while holding units in a pooled investment and three approved-unpaid grants
permitted_outcome: Fund Frozen; units are blocked property; grants without live attempts held; TVCTL-13 report filed; pool continues for other donors
prohibited_outcome: Grants paid or units redeemed for fees

scenario: REC-7 fresh step-up for a partner-federated donor is satisfied by the partner's own CIBA push
permitted_outcome: REC-7 step-up is sponsor-verified (TVR-WID-004 extended); partner assertion alone insufficient
prohibited_outcome: Partner-boundary confirmation satisfies REC-7. Note: REC-7 text should say 'sponsor-verified'

scenario: IRS revocation holds 140 grants; ATO attacker uses the 'redirect' option to route a held grant to a new attacker charity
permitted_outcome: Redirect is a new recommendation (Superseded) subject to recipient-novelty assurance and AUTH-I7
prohibited_outcome: Redirect handled as an amendment with lighter checks

scenario: Provider silently shortens its deduplication window from 72h to 24h; a retry at 30h is sent with the same key
permitted_outcome: PA-3 window is a monitored contract parameter; retries outside it need PA-2; PA-6 catches any double settlement
prohibited_outcome: Duplicate settled on assumed window

scenario: Bank's positive-pay service is down for a week in December; void confirmations cannot be obtained
permitted_outcome: Reissue only after Voided (PA-4); PA-5 aging escalates; charities told of delay
prohibited_outcome: Reissue before bank-confirmed stop

scenario: A $3M Lost claim must be written off; DoA requires board approval; board does not meet until February
permitted_outcome: Claim stays open; recognition per TIME-3/OD-19; write-off waits for DoA authority
prohibited_outcome: Staff write off under a lower threshold to close the year

scenario: TVCTL-13 blocking report clock runs over the holiday while the GC is unreachable
permitted_outcome: Named backup decider and time limit (TVR-OPS-006)
prohibited_outcome: Report missed

scenario: Board delegation for the routine path expires Dec 31 by its own terms; renewal not scheduled
permitted_outcome: TVCTL-09 suspends dependent policies at expiry; routine grants route to humans; renewal calendared outside peak
prohibited_outcome: Routine approvals continue under lapsed delegation

scenario: Sponsor A whitelists a sanctions false positive in a shared screening service; sponsor B's screening would inherit it
permitted_outcome: Tenant term: A's clearance never clears at B; B's own decision required
prohibited_outcome: Cross-tenant clearance

scenario: Family member in a fund dispute files repeated unauthenticated death notices for a living co-advisor
permitted_outcome: Each notice is a flag (AUTH-I5); repeated false notices recorded and escalated; Disputed AuthorityState governs
prohibited_outcome: Repeated notices hold the co-advisor indefinitely

scenario: Advisor is an employee of a large charity; TVCTL-14 routes every grant to that charity to humans in December
permitted_outcome: Human routing (TVCTL-14); queue capacity per TVF-162 staffing
prohibited_outcome: Relationship match overridden to clear backlog

scenario: Donor's agent token, issued before a suspicious credential change, keeps adding recipients during cooling-off
permitted_outcome: OD-14: agent-added new recipients always need principal confirmation; AUTH-I7 confirmation is sponsor-direct
prohibited_outcome: Agent recipients executed during cooling-off

scenario: A PA-6 double-payment case is open at fiscal year-end
permitted_outcome: Recognition and attribution per TIME-3/OD-19; disclosed as open item
prohibited_outcome: Case closed by assumption to finish the close

scenario: Model provider and screening vendor degrade together in the last week of December; fallbacks route most grants to humans
permitted_outcome: Fallback no less strict; backlog visible
prohibited_outcome: Release without screens

scenario: Primary provider fails with 3,000 Unknowns; ops want to fail over to the secondary rail
permitted_outcome: PA-1 blocks until PA-2 per attempt or bulk procedure
prohibited_outcome: Blind re-pay on secondary

scenario: Custodian placed in liquidation; pool assets frozen while grants are in Funding
permitted_outcome: Investment-structure transition workflow (TVF-122)
prohibited_outcome: Grants funded from other pools silently

scenario: Revocation of a terminated advisor's custodian trading authorization is delayed by the custodian's holiday closure
permitted_outcome: AUTH-I6 revocation SLA and evidence
prohibited_outcome: Trades continue

scenario: AG-17-extracted related-party links populate the TVCTL-14 relationship graph; an extraction miss lets a donor-controlled payee pass the 'deterministic' gate
permitted_outcome: Model extraction is an input needing verification before a D gate
prohibited_outcome: Probabilistic input treated as authoritative

scenario: Donor's mailbox is compromised; AUTH-I5/AUTH-I7 notices go to the attacker
permitted_outcome: Out-of-band channel diversity
prohibited_outcome: Notice to compromised channel counted as notice

scenario: Charity's verified contact mailbox is reassigned to a new employee who approves a bank change
permitted_outcome: Verified-channel residual risk
prohibited_outcome: Bank change accepted

scenario: Thin holiday rota: the second break-glass approver rubber-stamps
permitted_outcome: Randomized assignment, after-the-fact review
prohibited_outcome: Single-person break-glass in effect

scenario: Agent triggers dozens of REC-7 confirmations; donor approves all
permitted_outcome: Transaction-bound confirmation, batching limits
prohibited_outcome: Fatigue approval of injected recipient

scenario: Provider outage, custodian late file, model outage and staff holiday on Dec 30
permitted_outcome: Conjunction drills (TVR-OPS-003)
prohibited_outcome: Uncoordinated degradation

scenario: Attacker closes recipient account to force a return, then re-enrols a new account
permitted_outcome: Cooling-off on re-enrolment
prohibited_outcome: Re-pay to new account without cooling-off

scenario: AgentRun records lost in a restore; donor repudiates an agent grant
permitted_outcome: Evidence store DR tier
prohibited_outcome: Repudiation unresolvable

scenario: Sponsor A payee-hijack incident triggers a payments pause that also stops sponsor B
permitted_outcome: Tenant-scoped kill switch
prohibited_outcome: Cross-tenant halt

scenario: Sponsor chose B6's 're-derive security state from external sources' option. A restore loses 15 minutes of the sponsor's authorized-change log (the intent side of B19 matching). Re-derivation pulls factor enrolments from the IdP; legitimate enrolments made in the lost window now look unmatched, and an attacker enrolment made in the same window looks like one of them
permitted_outcome: Every re-derived credential or entitlement without a surviving authorization record stays blocked per record until re-authorized through a pre-change channel; the authorization records themselves are in the zero-loss tier
prohibited_outcome: Ops bulk-accept re-derived IdP state as 'lost legitimate changes' to clear false incidents, importing the attacker enrolment as authorized
finding_description: B6 allows security state to be re-derived from external registers, but B19 matching needs the sponsor's own record of authorized changes, which B6 does not place in the zero-loss tier. Requirement: the authorized-change records used for B19 matching are zero-loss; any re-derived external state with no surviving authorization record is treated as unmatched (incident, per-record block), never bulk-accepted.

scenario: Donor files a cancellation request and a fraud report through the verified channel; both are acknowledged on screen. A restore 6 minutes later loses both records. B6's zero-loss list names revocations, holds, cooling-off clocks and flags, not requests. The grant pays the next morning
permitted_outcome: Protective requests (cancellation, fraud report, stop request) are acknowledged only after durable commit in the zero-loss tier, or the post-restore reconciliation re-solicits them from requesters whose acknowledgements fall in the lost window
prohibited_outcome: Payment proceeds after the sponsor told the donor the request was received
finding_description: B1 and A12 make protective requests always available, but B6's zero-loss tier omits them. Requirement: add protective requests (cancellation, fraud report, stop/recall request) to the B6 zero-loss set; an acknowledgement is shown only after durable commit; post-restore, notify any requester whose acknowledged request may fall in the RPO window.

scenario: Command service is down on Dec 31. The B6 break-glass procedure (dual control) is invoked. Treasury asks to use it to release 200 Funded grants before year-end, since the procedure 'covers the period when the command service is down'
permitted_outcome: Break-glass during a command-service outage is limited to A12 protective actions (stop, recall, void, hold) and to recording observations; every break-glass action is replayed into the command log as a domain command on recovery before any further movement
prohibited_outcome: Money-moving releases under break-glass, bypassing SM-6 re-check, B8 snapshot verification and B18 destination confirmation
finding_description: B6 creates break-glass for the period when the command service is down; OD-22 permits break-glass only through a domain command, which cannot exist then. B6 also does not limit its scope. Requirement: outage break-glass is restricted to the A12 protective set and to observation recording; it cannot release, re-pay or change standing data; actions are replayed as domain commands with dual-control attribution before normal service resumes.

scenario: After a payee-hijack incident, the resume review re-verifies every payee, delegation and recovery change made inside the declared incident window (TVS-474). Forensics later show the attacker's first access was 19 days before the declared window start
permitted_outcome: Incident window start is set from the earliest indicator of compromise plus a defined look-back margin, and is re-opened when forensics move it; changes in the extended window are re-verified before their dependent payments
prohibited_outcome: Window fixed at detection time; earlier attacker changes are treated as clean
finding_description: No rule says how the incident window is bounded. Requirement: the review window starts at the earliest indicator of compromise minus a look-back margin [P]; it is a living parameter that re-opens re-verification when forensics move it.

scenario: B19 matching discovers that an IdP admin enrolled passkeys on 30 donor accounts over 10 days. During that time the sponsor saw no credential-change event, so B2 novelty and AUTH-I7 cooling-off never started, and recipients confirmed with those passkeys are now 'known'
permitted_outcome: On discovery, the unmatched enrolments are inserted retroactively as credential-change events; B2 novelty and AUTH-I7 are recomputed; recipients confirmed with the suspect factors become novel again; unpaid grants to them are held; paid ones get post-payment review
prohibited_outcome: Discovered unmatched enrolment is revoked going forward only; recipients it confirmed stay 'known'
finding_description: Same gap as M-4: post-incident state is not re-derived retroactively. Requirement: a discovered unmatched external change is back-dated into the sponsor's history, and every derived state (B2 novelty, AUTH-I7 clocks, confirmations, approvals under that assurance) is recomputed from that point.

scenario: An insider with DR operator rights declares a 'data corruption' incident and requests a point-in-time restore to 30 minutes earlier. The restore truncates the hash-chained evidence store (TVCTL-11) and removes the records of the insider's own approvals in that window, while B6 requires one consistent restore point including evidence
permitted_outcome: Restore is a dual-controlled action authorized outside the requester's line; the discarded tail of every store (especially evidence) is sealed and exported to a store outside the platform's administrative domain before restore; evidence is never truncated, only annotated
prohibited_outcome: Restore used as anti-forensics; consistent restore point erases evidence
finding_description: B6's consistent restore point includes the evidence store, so a restore can delete evidence. Nothing governs who may order a restore. Requirement: restores are dual-controlled with independent authorization; the pre-restore tail of each store is preserved and sealed off-platform; the evidence hash chain records the restore as an event and is never rolled back.

scenario: After a restore, the payment adapter's provider-key sequence counter rolls back and reissues key K, already used 4 minutes earlier for a different grant to the same charity (recurring instance). The provider returns 'already processed' with the earlier payment's Accepted result, and the new attempt is recorded as Accepted
permitted_outcome: Provider keys are globally unique and never derived from a restorable counter (e.g. include a restore epoch); a provider response is matched on key AND grant reference AND amount; a mismatch opens a PA-6 style case
prohibited_outcome: New grant shown as paid with another grant's evidence; B18 fingerprint matches because the charity is the same
finding_description: PA-3 requires a stable key but not a unique one across restores, and B18 cannot tell two payments to the same destination apart. Requirement: idempotency keys are never reissued after a restore; adapter contracts echo the sponsor's attempt reference and amount, and the gate compares all three.

scenario: After a provider-credential leak, webhook signing secrets and partner client registrations are rotated and the terminated partner's mTLS clients revoked. A week later a restore of the configuration store brings back the pre-rotation secrets and the revoked clients
permitted_outcome: Key material and client registrations move forward only: secret stores are excluded from point-in-time rollback and treated as B6 security state with zero-loss; any restore re-applies all rotations and revocations before traffic resumes
prohibited_outcome: Restore re-validates the attacker's stolen webhook secret and the terminated partner's clients
finding_description: B6's security state list (revocations, holds, clocks, flags) does not name keys, secrets and machine-client registrations. Requirement: rotations and revocations of keys, secrets, certificates and client registrations are zero-loss security state; no restore can roll them back.

scenario: A sponsor's DR design uses B6's re-derivation option for all security state. A model-raised hold and a human flag created 4 minutes before the outage have no external source to re-derive from
permitted_outcome: Internally originated holds and flags can only be zero-loss replicated; re-derivation applies only to state mastered externally
prohibited_outcome: Hold silently disappears because re-derivation found nothing

scenario: Restore loses the donor's sponsor-direct confirmations of three new recipients made in the RPO window; after restore their recommendations look unconfirmed
permitted_outcome: Lost confirmations are treated as absent: re-confirmation required (fail-safe); donor told why
prohibited_outcome: Confirmation assumed from the restored recommendation record

scenario: Payee and policy stores restore to a different point from decisioning; B8 then finds decision snapshots citing payee and policy versions absent from the restored history
permitted_outcome: B6 consistent restore point covers standing-data and policy stores; missing versions are per-record blocks pending reconciliation, never treated as 'not reverted'
prohibited_outcome: B8 passes because the cited version is simply missing from history

scenario: An attacker socially engineers the sponsor's bank support and gains a portal user. They mark three altered checks (same check number and amount, payee name changed) as 'pay' in the positive-pay exception queue. TVCTL-07 matches each debit to an outstanding check by number and amount. Entitlements are reviewed quarterly (B19)
permitted_outcome: Bank-portal actions (positive-pay exception decisions, user and entitlement changes) are streamed daily and matched to platform decisions; payee-name positive pay is required; an exception decision with no platform decision is an incident
prohibited_outcome: Portal decision made outside the platform is honoured; periodic entitlement review is the only control
finding_description: B19 covers bank-portal entitlements only through periodic review, while custodian and IdP actions are matched daily. Portal actions are themselves payment decisions. Requirement: bank-portal actions (positive-pay exception decisions, ACH debit-filter changes, wire templates, user and limit changes) are matched to authorized platform commands daily; payee-name positive pay on disbursement accounts.

scenario: A portal user removes the ACH debit block on the disbursement account and adds a wire template; an outside originator then debits the account twice. TVCTL-07 flags the unmatched debits next day; the debit-block change itself was never seen
permitted_outcome: Debit-filter and template changes are matched like other B19 register actions on the day they occur
prohibited_outcome: Control change detected only through its first loss
finding_description: As M-7: bank-portal configuration changes are an external register not matched to authorized commands.

scenario: Through the custodian portal, an attacker changes the standing settlement instruction for the pool's cash sweep to an outside account. The next authorized sweep command executes; B19's daily match pairs the movement with the authorized command on amount and date, and the movement is 'matched'
permitted_outcome: Custodian and bank standing instructions (SSIs, sweep destinations, wire templates) are register entries whose changes are matched to authorized commands; B19 matching compares destination as well as amount; destination mismatch blocks and opens an incident
prohibited_outcome: Authorized command plus attacker-changed destination counts as matched
finding_description: B19 matches custodian movements to commands but does not require destination comparison, and settlement instructions held at the custodian are not named as a register. It is the custody equivalent of B18. Requirement: the sponsor holds its own verified copy of custodian and bank settlement instructions; each movement is matched on destination; SSI changes need dual control and are matched to an authorized change.

scenario: A portal user submits a tender-offer election for a pooled position at the custodian. No asset moves until settlement 3 weeks later, so B19's daily movement matching sees nothing until then
permitted_outcome: Pending custodian instructions and elections are visible and matched to authorized commands on the day they are entered
prohibited_outcome: Election discovered only at settlement
finding_description: As M-8: B19 matches movements, not pending instructions. Requirement: the custodian's pending-instruction register is matched daily.

scenario: An attacker with IdP admin adds a new federated identity source that can assert any sponsor user, and lowers the MFA policy for one group. No factor enrolment or admin grant occurs
permitted_outcome: IdP configuration changes (federation trusts, policies, signing keys, session lifetimes) are administrative actions matched to authorized changes under B19; unmatched is an incident
prohibited_outcome: Only enrolments and admin grants matched

scenario: The provider is compromised (TVS-624). The attacker changes the account behind a charity token and makes the provider return the cached original account fingerprint with each payment. B18 compares the echoed fingerprint with sponsor-held data and finds a match
permitted_outcome: The destination evidence comes from a party independent of the provider register: a receiving-bank name or account-confirmation result, or beneficiary data on the sponsor's own bank record, plus periodic charity confirmation of receipt; a provider-computed fingerprint alone detects provider errors only
prohibited_outcome: B18 accepted as satisfied by a provider-computed fingerprint in the provider-compromise threat model it was written for
finding_description: B18 accepts 'account fingerprint or name-match result', but a fingerprint computed by the provider is controlled by the party whose compromise B18 is meant to detect. Requirement: at least one destination confirmation per payment, or per sample, comes from outside the provider (receiving-bank confirmation, sponsor-bank beneficiary data, or charity receipt confirmation); adapter contracts state which source each fingerprint comes from.

scenario: The registrar account for the sponsor's domain is taken over. The attacker changes MX records and obtains a valid TLS certificate. Sponsor-direct confirmations (B20), charity bank-change verifications and prior-channel notices sent 'from the sponsor' now route through the attacker
permitted_outcome: Registrar, DNS, certificate issuance (CAA, certificate-transparency monitoring) and SMS sender registrations are external registers under B19: changes are matched to authorized changes daily; registrar lock and dual control; an unmatched change suspends sponsor-direct confirmations until verified
prohibited_outcome: Sponsor-direct channel assumed independent while its naming infrastructure is attacker-controlled
finding_description: Every 'sponsor-direct' and 'verified channel' control assumes the sponsor's own domain and messaging identities are intact. None is in B19's register list. Requirement: add domain registrar, DNS, certificate issuance and messaging sender identities to B19 external registers, with lock, CT monitoring and daily matching.

scenario: B18 blocks 400 payments in December because the provider shows new destination accounts. Charities updated them through the provider's self-service portal. Ops propose updating the sponsor's verified store from the provider values to clear the queue
permitted_outcome: A B18 mismatch is resolved only by CW-06 verification of the new destination by the sponsor (prior-contact notice, cooling-off); provider-wide mismatches go to the B15 bulk-triage procedure with dual control and sampling; provider self-service changes are contractually disabled or reported
prohibited_outcome: Provider value copied into the sponsor's verified store, turning an unverified change into 'verified'
finding_description: B18 defines the block but not how a mismatch is resolved; the obvious remedy (accept the provider's value) undoes B11 and B18. Requirement: a mismatch is resolved only through sponsor-side CW-06 verification with cooling-off; bulk mismatches are handled as an incident; provider contracts disable or report charity self-service account changes.

scenario: The provider changes its fingerprint format during a vault migration; every B18 comparison mismatches; ops ask to switch B18 off until January
permitted_outcome: Switching off B18 is a loosening that needs Change Board and CRCO approval with an expiry (TVS-478 rule); provider format changes need contractual notice; payments wait
prohibited_outcome: Control disabled informally under year-end pressure

scenario: The custodian's own systems are breached and pool securities are moved out by a custodian insider. The custodian's daily movement and position files, the source for B19 matching and NAV, omit the movements
permitted_outcome: At least one position or movement source is independent of the custodian (sub-custodian or depository participant statements, independent confirmation, administrator records), reconciled at a stated frequency; a custodian-sourced break is never resolved by custodian data alone
prohibited_outcome: B19 match and NAV rely only on reports from the register holder that is compromised
finding_description: Provider evidence is checked against the sponsor's bank; custody has no independent second source in any control. Requirement: periodic independent confirmation of custody positions and movements [P frequency], with source independence declared per register.

scenario: The sponsor meets B12 with two banks, but both outsource core processing to the same processor, which suffers a multi-day outage on Dec 28
permitted_outcome: Redundancy is assessed for shared fourth parties (core processor, cloud region, payment network access, screening vendor); B12's second bank must not share critical dependencies
prohibited_outcome: Two banks counted as redundant while sharing one point of failure
finding_description: B12 counts banks, not independent infrastructure. Requirement: a fourth-party dependency register for banks, providers, custodians and model vendors; redundancy and exposure limits are computed per shared dependency.

scenario: Each of two providers is within its B16 in-transit cap, but both hold pre-funded balances at the same FBO bank, which fails; the combined exposure is twice what reserves cover
permitted_outcome: B16 exposure is also aggregated per common dependency (FBO bank, provider parent); reserves and insurance are sized to the aggregate
prohibited_outcome: Per-provider caps satisfied while aggregate exposure to one bank is uncapped
finding_description: As M-12: B16 caps per provider, not per shared dependency.

scenario: The payment provider is acquired. Webhook signing keys, charity tokens and bank data move to the acquirer's platform, and routing changes. Settlement evidence keeps arriving with valid signatures, so B15 keeps grading it 'authenticated'
permitted_outcome: A change of control, insolvency filing or receivership at a third party automatically lowers the grade of its evidence (B15), triggers key rotation and re-attestation of the adapter contract (A10), reduces its B16 cap, and samples B18 confirmations more often
prohibited_outcome: Valid signature taken as proof of the same trustworthy counterparty
finding_description: No rule reacts to changes in who controls a third party. Requirement: third-party change-of-control or insolvency events are monitored contract triggers; they re-grade the party's evidence and require re-attestation before full trust is restored.

scenario: The payment provider is a bank-sponsored fintech whose sponsor bank also holds the sponsor's disbursement account; both 'sources' in PA-2 and the A10 per-item reconciliation come from systems under common control
permitted_outcome: Sources under common control count as one source; if no independent second source exists, only ResolvedByDecision is available (A10 rule); adapter contract declares control relationships
prohibited_outcome: PA-2 two-source proof met by two feeds from one institution
finding_description: PA-2 and A10 count sources, not independent sources. Requirement: each adapter contract declares the ownership and control relationships among its evidence sources; sources under common control satisfy only one side of the two-source proof.

scenario: The model provider's serving stack is compromised; AG-02 returns well-formed Result(valid) 'no benefit indicators' for every grant
permitted_outcome: Model can only add flags, never approve; seeded cases (CTL-046) detect the recall collapse; deterministic rules still run
prohibited_outcome: Valid-schema output treated as a clearance

scenario: The sanctions screening vendor's list feed is tampered with to drop one SDN entry
permitted_outcome: CTL-050 cross-check against an independent list source; data-freshness and hash checks; TVCTL-04 at release
prohibited_outcome: Single-source list accepted

scenario: The disbursement bank fails; the bridge bank honours checks using a stale positive-pay file, so a check already bank-confirmed as voided (A8, commitment restored and reissued) is paid
permitted_outcome: Contradicting evidence after Voided opens a PA-6 double-payment case; B12 contingency covers outstanding checks; OD-20 loss bearer
prohibited_outcome: Void treated as final; second payment unnoticed

scenario: A partner firm fails; its domain lapses and is re-registered; advisors' recovery email addresses are on that domain; the partner IdP is gone
permitted_outcome: Partner-exit re-proofing with sponsor-direct factors and cooling-off; recovery through a recycled domain is not trusted
prohibited_outcome: Account recovery through recycled-domain email

scenario: The provider's receiver claims the sponsor's pre-funded balance as estate property, not trust funds
permitted_outcome: PA-8 receivable; B16 cap sized to reserves; OD-20 loss-bearer policy
prohibited_outcome: Fund cash assumed safe

scenario: Attackers spread additions of one sham charity across 9 months, staying under the B3 count per period; 120 donors eventually recommend to it
permitted_outcome: Recipient fan-in measured cumulatively (decaying or since first seen at the sponsor), weighted by the recipient's age and by value, not as a count in a fixed period
prohibited_outcome: Fixed-period count that low-and-slow additions stay under
finding_description: B3 repeats the waitable-window pattern that B2 removed for novelty. Requirement: the B3 signal is cumulative from the recipient's first appearance at the sponsor, weighted by value and recipient age; the period is not a reset.

scenario: The B16 cap is checked against end-of-day in-transit balances. Pre-funding happens each morning and settlement each afternoon. Over the Dec 24-28 holiday the pre-funded balance sits for four days at three times the cap
permitted_outcome: Exposure is measured at peak intraday and over the full non-settlement horizon, including scheduled pre-funding; pre-funding is refused if it would breach the cap
prohibited_outcome: EOD snapshot hides intraday and holiday exposure
finding_description: B16 does not say when exposure is measured. Requirement: the cap is a pre-transfer check against projected peak exposure through the next settlement date on the rail calendar.

scenario: A per-donor daily velocity cap uses a fixed calendar day (UTC). An ATO attacker submits the cap's worth at 23:50 and again at 00:10
permitted_outcome: Velocity and aggregate thresholds use sliding windows
prohibited_outcome: Fixed windows allow twice the cap across a boundary
finding_description: TIME-1 names calendars and zones but not window type. Requirement: security velocity and aggregate thresholds are sliding windows; fixed periods only for reporting.

scenario: An ATO attacker splits $90k into four $22.5k recommendations from the donor's four funds to the same new recipient, each below the step-up threshold
permitted_outcome: REC-7 cross-fund flag; aggregate per-recipient thresholds per principal across funds (TVF-075); B20 device-bound confirmation for a new recipient
prohibited_outcome: Per-fund threshold evaluation

scenario: An attacker takes over the account through a synced passkey (no event) or waits out the AUTH-I7 cooling-off after enrolling a factor, then adds a co-advisor they control. The co-advisor's channels are all new, so under B2 the co-advisor's first device-bound confirmation makes its recipients 'known'
permitted_outcome: Authority grants (co-advisor, delegate, agent, successor) are confirmed through a sponsor-direct channel that existed before the granting principal's most recent credential change; the new principal's recipients are novel until confirmed by a pre-existing principal or channel
prohibited_outcome: Waiting out the cooling-off lets the attacker add a new principal whose own channels launder recipient novelty
finding_description: B2 fixed waiting-out for recipients but not for authority grants. Adding a principal creates a fresh set of 'pre-existing' channels. Requirement: B2's channel-predating rule also applies to authority grants; a principal added by a session whose assurance comes from post-change credentials cannot make recipients known.

scenario: A fraudster funds a DAF by ACH debit from a victim's account, waits until the rail return window has passed (Final), then grants to a sham charity; the victim's bank later pursues a warranty claim
permitted_outcome: Final(rail) is not treated as legal finality; CON-3 sponsor receivable and case on later reversal; provisional limit for new donors 0 (OD-04); novelty checks apply to the grant
prohibited_outcome: Contribution Final means value is irreversible

scenario: A grant of 'the proceeds of my stock gift' passes the routine path on an estimated $20k; the volatile asset sells (A6 net proceeds) for $180k, above the routine threshold and the DoA limit
permitted_outcome: Routine-path threshold and DoA limits are re-evaluated when a proceeds-linked, percentage or residual amount is fixed; above the threshold, the grant routes to a human before payment
prohibited_outcome: Routine decision on an estimate carries over to a fixed amount nine times larger
finding_description: SM-6 re-checks authority, eligibility, holds and freshness, not amount thresholds; A6 fixes the amount after approval. Requirement: amount-dependent routing (routine threshold, DoA tier, step-up tier) is re-evaluated at fixing.

scenario: An attacker-controlled charity accepts a grant, returns it citing an FX difference, is re-paid with an A7 top-up, and repeats the cycle
permitted_outcome: A second return on the same grant opens a case; A7 top-ups are capped cumulatively per grant; re-payment after a return is a recorded human decision
prohibited_outcome: Repeated exempt top-ups drain the fund
finding_description: A7 caps the top-up per return, not across cycles. Requirement: cumulative cap across return and re-payment cycles; a repeat return requires post-payment review (A18).

scenario: A requester puts phrases in a grant purpose that reliably trigger the model provider's safety filter, forcing the B13 deterministic fallback, which is weaker at benefit detection (FMEA-09 residual)
permitted_outcome: A forced-fallback rate is tracked per requester and recipient; when an agent refuses because of requester-supplied content, the grant goes to a human, not to the deterministic pass
prohibited_outcome: Requester can choose the weaker screen
finding_description: B13 makes the fallback safe on average, but the requester can trigger it. Requirement: non-Result outcomes caused by requester content route to human review; fallback rates per actor are monitored.

scenario: During detected clock skew, A12 keeps 'recording external observations' available. A return notice is recorded with a skewed recorded time that precedes its settlement notice, and a Final(rail) computation uses the skewed time
permitted_outcome: Observations recorded while skew is detected are tagged time-untrusted, are re-timed from the authoritative source or provider timestamp, and are excluded from deadline and ordering computations (Final, PA-6 ordering, cooling-off) until re-timed
prohibited_outcome: Protective availability corrupts ordering and finality
finding_description: A12 exempts observation recording from fail-closed without saying which clock stamps it. Requirement: time-untrusted marking and re-timing before any derived deadline or ordering decision uses the record.

scenario: After a B4 bulk remap of 40,000 partner users, it is unclear whether the remap counts as a 'credential change' for B2. If it does, every recipient confirmed only through the old partner channel becomes novel in December. If it does not, a mis-mapped subject inherits another donor's 'known' recipients
permitted_outcome: The remap is a credential-change event for B2 and AUTH-I7; recipients confirmed through a sponsor-direct channel stay known; B4 first-use step-up is sponsor-verified; mapping errors are caught by attested pairs
prohibited_outcome: Undefined interaction decided ad hoc at peak
finding_description: B2 and B4 do not say how they interact. Requirement: define an identifier remap as a credential-change event for novelty, and schedule bulk remaps outside the year-end freeze (B14 analogue).

scenario: At cutover B7 makes 9,000 imported payees Unverified. Ops email charities asking them to 're-submit bank details', the same re-enrolment pattern that B11 was written to avoid; lookalike phishing follows
permitted_outcome: Imported details are verified by sponsor-initiated confirmation of what the incumbent held (name-match, pre-note, outbound call to a known contact); charities are never asked to send new details; communications are pre-announced through a known channel
prohibited_outcome: Re-collection at migration recreates the TVS-612 phishing surface
finding_description: B7 requires re-verification but not how. Requirement: payee verification after migration confirms the existing data and never asks charities to re-submit it.

scenario: A grant approved under policy P-10 waits in ApprovedAwaitingCapacity until December. P-14 has since tightened the threshold, and B8 flags only reverted versions
permitted_outcome: The decision stands under the version in force at decision; superseded is not reverted
prohibited_outcome: Retroactive decline

scenario: An attacker floods the B15 triage queue with unauthenticated settlement claims; a genuine single-source duplicate report from a charity's verified contact sits unreviewed past the PA-6 recovery window
permitted_outcome: Triage items have an SLA and escalate (FLAG-1 analogue); they never close by time; queue flooding by source is rate-limited and alerted
prohibited_outcome: Real contradiction lost in triage
finding_description: B15 creates a triage queue with no aging rule. Requirement: triage items carry an SLA, owner and escalation, and are prioritized by source grade.

scenario: Funds blocked at an intermediary (B9) sit for years as a blocked receivable from the provider path; it is unclear whether they count toward the B16 in-transit cap
permitted_outcome: Blocked receivables are excluded from the provider's operational cap but tracked against sponsor reserves and disclosed
prohibited_outcome: Blocked amounts either fill the cap indefinitely or are hidden
finding_description: B9 and B16 do not say how they interact. Requirement: define how blocked receivables are treated in exposure caps and reserves.

scenario: A compromised or malicious sponsor tenant issues B5 fraud warnings against five large charities on Dec 20; holds appear in every tenant
permitted_outcome: A cross-tenant warning raises a flag for local review, and a hold only when it carries sanctions-grade or verified evidence; warnings are attributed and rate-limited; local review SLA; the issuing tenant is accountable for false warnings
prohibited_outcome: Cross-tenant warnings used as a cross-sponsor denial of service at year-end
finding_description: B5 restricts what a warning can clear, but not who can raise holds at scale. Requirement: attribution, rate limits, and evidence grading for cross-tenant warnings; non-sanctions warnings flag rather than hold.

scenario: The same sham charity is added by a few donors at each of eight sponsors on the platform; each sponsor's B3 monitor stays below threshold
permitted_outcome: A platform-level fan-in signal is a B5 warning: it can raise flags in each tenant but decides nothing
prohibited_outcome: Tenant isolation prevents any cross-sponsor signal
